source.text: Καὶ εὐθὺς πρωῒ συμβούλιον ποιήσαντες οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς μετὰ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων καὶ γραμματέων καὶ ὅλον τὸ συνέδριον δήσαντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπήνεγκαν καὶ παρέδωκαν Πιλάτῳ.

records.literal_gloss: And immediately early a council having made the chief priests with the elders and scribes and all the Council, having bound Jesus they led [him] away and handed [him] over to Pilate.

en.L: And immediately, early in the morning, the chief priests, having held a council with the elders and scribes and the whole Council, bound Jesus, led [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] away, and handed [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] over to Pilate.
en.B: As soon as it was morning, the chief priests met with the elders, the scribes and the whole Council and reached a decision. They bound Jesus, led {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} off, and handed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to Pilate.
en.R: Very early in the morning, the leading priests met with the leaders of the people, the teachers of God's law, and the whole Jewish council. They made their plan. They tied Jesus up and led {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} away. Then they handed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to Pilate, the Roman governor.

es.L: Y en seguida, de madrugada, los jefes de los sacerdotes, habiendo deliberado con los ancianos y [los] escribas y todo el concilio, ataron a Jesús, [{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}] llevaron y [{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}] entregaron a Pilato.
es.B: En cuanto amaneció, los jefes de los sacerdotes se reunieron con los ancianos, los escribas y todo el Consejo, y tomaron una decisión. Ataron a Jesús, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llevaron y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} entregaron a Pilato.
es.R: Muy temprano por la mañana, los jefes de los sacerdotes se reunieron con los ancianos que dirigían al pueblo, con los maestros de la ley y con todo el Consejo Supremo de los judíos. Hicieron su plan. Ataron a Jesús y se {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llevaron. Luego {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} entregaron a Pilato, el gobernador romano.

sw.L: Na mara moja, alfajiri, wakuu wa makuhani, wakiisha kufanya shauri pamoja na wazee na waandishi na baraza zima, walimfunga Yesu, wakamchukua, wakamkabidhi kwa Pilato.
sw.B: Kulipopambazuka tu, wakuu wa makuhani walikutana na wazee, waandishi na baraza zima, wakafikia uamuzi. Wakamfunga Yesu, wakamchukua, wakamkabidhi kwa Pilato.
sw.R: Asubuhi na mapema sana, wakuu wa makuhani walikutana na wazee waliowaongoza watu, walimu wa sheria na baraza kuu lote la Wayahudi. Wakapanga mpango wao. Wakamfunga Yesu, wakamchukua. Kisha wakamkabidhi kwa Pilato, mkuu wa mkoa wa Kirumi.

decisions.choice: having held a council: they met and reached a decision
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean to hold a meeting or to come to a decision, as in 3:6. After the night hearing (14:53-65), the leaders meet at dawn to agree on what to do with Jesus. Some manuscripts read "having prepared" a decision instead of "having made" one. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: chief priests, elders, scribes, the whole Council: the ruling Jewish council in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: These groups together made up the Sanhedrin, the council that met under the high priest (8:31; 14:53, 55).

decisions.choice: Pilate: Pontius Pilate, the Roman governor of Judea
decisions.reason: Pilate governed Judea for Rome from about AD 26 to 36. Under Roman rule the council could not carry out a death sentence on its own, so they brought Jesus to him.

decisions.choice: handed over: the word of Jesus' predictions
decisions.reason: Jesus had said the Son of Man would be handed over to the chief priests and that they would hand him over to the Gentiles (10:33). Now it happens.

decisions.choice: handed over
decisions.reason: All levels keep "handed over", the phrase used in the passion predictions (9:31; 10:33). Readable also calls the council "the whole Jewish council" and says who Pilate was.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans on the separate pronouns and possessives (lo, le, él, su, ti, tú, sí, me, mío); none on pronouns joined to the verb (crucifícalo, saludarlo) or where Spanish leaves the subject out
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually drops the subject pronoun where English says "he", and a pronoun joined to the verb cannot take a capital, so the setting covers fewer words than in English. As in Matthew 26-27; this holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: los jefes de los sacerdotes; los ancianos (L, B), los ancianos que dirigían al pueblo (R); los escribas (L, B), los maestros de la ley (R); el concilio (L), el Consejo (B), el Consejo Supremo (R); entregar
decisions.reason: The terms used for these groups across the New Testament drafts, as in Matthew 26:57-59, recorded once in this chapter (meaning decision m2). Every level says "entregar", the verb of Jesus's predictions (meaning decision m4), here and in verses 10 and 15.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span on the verbs (wakamchukua, wakamkabidhi); spans on free pronouns and possessives only (yake, wake, chake, zake, naye, wewe, yeye, mwenyewe, wangu)
alternatives: a span wherever the English has one
decisions.reason: The English "him" takes the setting. Swahili carries it in the verb's object prefix -m-, which cannot take a capital, so Swahili has fewer spans than English throughout the chapter, as in Matthew 26-27.

decisions.choice: wakuu wa makuhani; wazee (L, B), wazee waliowaongoza watu (R); waandishi (L, B), walimu wa sheria (R); baraza (L, B), baraza kuu (R); kukabidhi
decisions.reason: The terms used for these groups across the New Testament drafts, as in Matthew 26:57-59, recorded once in this chapter (meaning decision m2). Every level says "kukabidhi" (hand over), the verb of the passion in John 19 and of Jesus's predictions (meaning decision m4), here and in verses 10 and 15.

source.text: καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτὸν ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Σὺ εἶ ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων;

records.literal_gloss: And questioned him Pilate, You are the King of the Jews?

en.L: And Pilate questioned {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the King of the Jews?"
en.B: Pilate questioned {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "So {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the King of the Jews?"
en.R: Pilate asked Jesus, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the king of the Jewish people?"

es.L: Y Pilato {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntó: «¿Eres {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} el Rey de los judíos?».
es.B: Pilato {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntó: «¿Así que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} eres el Rey de los judíos?».
es.R: Pilato le preguntó a Jesús: «¿Eres {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} el rey del pueblo judío?».

sw.L: Na Pilato akamwuliza, "Je, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ndiwe Mfalme wa Wayahudi?"
sw.B: Pilato alimwuliza, "Basi, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ndiwe Mfalme wa Wayahudi?"
sw.R: Pilato alimwuliza Yesu, "Je, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ni mfalme wa Wayahudi?"

decisions.choice: the King of the Jews: a political charge
decisions.reason: To Pilate a man claiming to be king without Rome's approval was a rebel against Caesar. The council had asked whether Jesus was the Messiah (14:61); before Pilate the charge becomes kingship.

decisions.choice: You are: the pronoun is stressed
decisions.reason: Pilate says "you" with emphasis: you, this prisoner, are the king?

decisions.choice: the king of the Jewish people
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words. Literal and Balanced keep the title as it stands on the charge in 15:26.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτῷ λέγει· Σὺ λέγεις.

records.literal_gloss: And answering him he says, You say.

en.L: And answering him, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says, "You say [so]."
en.B: He answered him, "You have said so."
en.R: Jesus answered, "Those are your words."

es.L: Y respondiéndole, dice: «Tú [lo] dices».
es.B: Él le respondió: «Tú lo has dicho».
es.R: Jesús le contestó: «Eso lo dices tú».

sw.L: Naye, akimjibu, anasema, "Wewe unasema [hivyo]."
sw.B: Alimjibu, "Wewe umesema hivyo."
sw.R: Yesu alijibu, "Hayo ni maneno yako wewe."

decisions.choice: he says: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: Mark often tells past events in the present tense to make them vivid. The sense is past.

decisions.choice: You say: a reply that accepts the title but leaves it in Pilate's mouth
decisions.reason: Jesus does not deny it, but he does not take up Pilate's meaning either. Before the council he answered "I am" (14:62). Here his reply is guarded: the words are true, but the kind of king Pilate fears is not what Jesus is. Some take it as a simple yes.

decisions.choice: You: stressed, it is Pilate who says it
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out, putting weight on Pilate as the speaker.

decisions.choice: You have said so (B); Those are your words (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the guarded form of the answer and do not turn it into a plain yes.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (dice); past at Balanced and Readable (respondió, contestó)
decisions.reason: Mark tells much of this chapter in the present (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past, as Spanish narrative does. The same in verses 16, 17, 20, 21, 22, 24 and 27.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (anasema); narrative past at Balanced and Readable, -li- for the first verb of a sequence and -ka- for those that follow
decisions.reason: Mark tells much of this chapter in the present (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the narrative past. The same in verses 16, 17, 20, 21, 22, 24 and 27.

source.text: καὶ κατηγόρουν αὐτοῦ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς πολλά.

records.literal_gloss: And were accusing him the chief priests of many things.

en.L: And the chief priests were accusing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} of many things.
en.B: The chief priests kept bringing many charges against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: The leading priests kept accusing Jesus of many things.

es.L: Y los jefes de los sacerdotes {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} acusaban de muchas cosas.
es.B: Los jefes de los sacerdotes presentaban contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} una acusación tras otra.
es.R: Los jefes de los sacerdotes seguían acusando a Jesús de muchas cosas.

sw.L: Na wakuu wa makuhani walikuwa wakimshtaki mambo mengi.
sw.B: Wakuu wa makuhani waliendelea kuleta mashtaka mengi dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.R: Wakuu wa makuhani waliendelea kumshtaki Yesu kwa mambo mengi.

decisions.choice: were accusing: an ongoing action, charge after charge
decisions.reason: The tense pictures the accusations going on.

decisions.choice: many things: many charges, or with much insistence
decisions.reason: The word can mean many things or can mean strongly. Pilate's words in 15:4 ("how many things") show that many charges are meant.

decisions.choice: kept bringing many charges
decisions.reason: Balanced brings out the ongoing tense.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος πάλιν ἐπηρώτα αὐτὸν λέγων· Οὐκ ἀποκρίνῃ οὐδέν;

records.literal_gloss: And Pilate again was questioning him, saying, Not you answer nothing?

en.L: And Pilate again questioned {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not answer anything?
en.B: So Pilate put another question to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: "Have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} no answer at all?
en.R: So Pilate asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} again, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not going to answer?

es.L: Y Pilato {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} interrogaba de nuevo, diciendo: «¿No respondes nada?
es.B: Así que Pilato {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} hizo otra pregunta: «¿No tienes nada que responder?
es.R: Entonces Pilato {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntó otra vez: «¿No vas a responder?

sw.L: Naye Pilato akamwuliza tena, akisema, "Hujibu chochote?
sw.B: Basi Pilato alimwuliza swali jingine: "Huna jibu lolote?
sw.R: Kwa hiyo Pilato alimwuliza tena, "Hutajibu?

decisions.choice: not ... nothing: a double negative, expecting him to answer
alternatives: a statement that he did not answer
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer that Jesus surely will reply. The two negatives strengthen each other.

decisions.choice: was questioning: Pilate pressed him more than once
decisions.reason: The tense suggests repeated questioning.

decisions.choice: Have you no answer at all? (B); Are you not going to answer? (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the question in natural English.

source.text: ἴδε πόσα σου κατηγοροῦσιν.

records.literal_gloss: See how many things you they are accusing.

en.L: See how many things they are accusing {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} of."
en.B: Look at all the charges they are bringing against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."
en.R: Listen to all the things they say {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have done!"

es.L: Mira de cuántas cosas {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} acusan».
es.B: Mira todas las acusaciones que presentan contra {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}».
es.R: ¡Escucha todo lo que dicen que has hecho!».

sw.L: Tazama ni mambo mangapi wanayokushtaki."
sw.B: Tazama mashtaka yote wanayoleta dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}."
sw.R: Sikiliza mambo yote wanayosema umefanya!"

decisions.choice: See: look, pay attention
decisions.reason: The word draws attention, like "look".

decisions.choice: how many things: an exclamation
decisions.reason: Pilate is not asking the number. He points to the weight of the charges.

decisions.choice: Listen to
decisions.reason: The charges were spoken, so Readable says "listen".

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς οὐκέτι οὐδὲν ἀπεκρίθη, ὥστε θαυμάζειν τὸν Πιλᾶτον.

records.literal_gloss: But Jesus no longer nothing answered, so as to amaze Pilate.

en.L: But Jesus no longer answered anything, so that Pilate was amazed.
en.B: But Jesus made no further reply at all, and Pilate was astonished.
en.R: But Jesus still did not say a word. Pilate was very surprised.

es.L: Pero Jesús ya no respondió nada, de modo que Pilato se asombraba.
es.B: Pero Jesús no volvió a responder nada, y Pilato quedó asombrado.
es.R: Pero Jesús seguía sin decir ni una palabra. Pilato se quedó muy sorprendido.

sw.L: Lakini Yesu hakujibu tena neno lolote, hata Pilato akashangaa.
sw.B: Lakini Yesu hakujibu tena hata neno moja, naye Pilato akastaajabu.
sw.R: Lakini Yesu bado hakusema neno lolote. Pilato alishangaa sana.

decisions.choice: no longer answered anything: the silence of the suffering servant
alternatives: he did not hear the question
decisions.reason: Isaiah 53:7 says the servant did not open his mouth, like a lamb led to the slaughter. Jesus had also kept silent before the high priest (14:61).

decisions.choice: no longer nothing: a strong double negative
decisions.reason: After his short answer in 15:2 he said nothing more at all.

decisions.choice: amazed: surprised, wondering
decisions.reason: Pilate was surprised that a man facing death would not defend himself.

decisions.choice: still did not say a word
decisions.reason: Readable uses everyday words for the double negative.

source.text: Κατὰ δὲ ἑορτὴν ἀπέλυεν αὐτοῖς ἕνα δέσμιον ὃν παρῃτοῦντο.

records.literal_gloss: Now at [the] feast he used to release to them one prisoner whom they requested.

en.L: Now at [the] feast he used to release to them one prisoner whom they requested.
en.B: At the festival it was his custom to set free for them one prisoner of their choosing.
en.R: Every year at the Passover festival, Pilate would set one prisoner free. The people could choose which one.

es.L: Ahora bien, en [la] fiesta les soltaba un preso, el que pedían.
es.B: En la fiesta tenía la costumbre de dejarles libre a un preso, el que ellos escogieran.
es.R: Cada año, en la fiesta de la Pascua, Pilato ponía en libertad a un preso. La gente podía escoger cuál.

sw.L: Basi wakati wa sikukuu alikuwa akiwafungulia mfungwa mmoja waliyemwomba.
sw.B: Wakati wa sikukuu ilikuwa desturi yake kuwafungulia mfungwa mmoja waliyemchagua.
sw.R: Kila mwaka wakati wa sikukuu ya Pasaka, Pilato alikuwa akimwachilia huru mfungwa mmoja. Watu waliweza kuchagua ni yupi.

decisions.choice: the feast: the Passover festival
decisions.reason: Mark has been telling of the Passover since 14:1. The custom belonged to this feast.

decisions.choice: used to release: a custom, done each year
decisions.reason: The tense describes what Pilate did regularly.

decisions.choice: the release of a prisoner: a custom known only from the Gospels
decisions.reason: No other ancient writer mentions this custom, but all four Gospels do (John 18:39). It was a favor to the people at their festival.

decisions.choice: Every year at the Passover festival
decisions.reason: Readable names the feast and makes the custom clear.

source.text: ἦν δὲ ὁ λεγόμενος Βαραββᾶς μετὰ τῶν στασιαστῶν δεδεμένος οἵτινες ἐν τῇ στάσει φόνον πεποιήκεισαν.

records.literal_gloss: Now there was the [one] called Barabbas with the rebels bound, who in the insurrection murder had committed.

en.L: Now there was the one called Barabbas, bound with the rebels who had committed murder in the insurrection.
en.B: A man named Barabbas was in prison along with the rebels who had killed people in the uprising.
en.R: A man named Barabbas was in prison at that time. He was with some men who had fought against the Romans. They had killed people during a riot.

es.L: Y estaba el llamado Barrabás, preso con los sediciosos que en la revuelta habían cometido homicidio.
es.B: Un hombre llamado Barrabás estaba preso junto con los rebeldes que habían matado a gente durante la revuelta.
es.R: En ese tiempo estaba en la cárcel un hombre llamado Barrabás. Estaba con unos hombres que se habían levantado contra los romanos. Habían matado a gente durante un motín.

sw.L: Basi alikuwepo yule aitwaye Baraba, amefungwa pamoja na waasi waliokuwa wamefanya mauaji katika uasi.
sw.B: Mtu mmoja aitwaye Baraba alikuwa gerezani pamoja na waasi waliokuwa wameua watu wakati wa uasi.
sw.R: Wakati huo mtu mmoja aitwaye Baraba alikuwa gerezani. Alikuwa pamoja na watu waliopigana na Warumi. Watu hao walikuwa wameua watu wakati wa ghasia.

decisions.choice: Barabbas: an Aramaic name meaning son of the father
decisions.reason: Bar means son and abba means father. It was a family name, not a title.

decisions.choice: rebels, the insurrection: men who rose up against Roman rule
decisions.reason: The word means an uprising. The definite article points to an uprising Mark's readers knew of, though no other source names it.

decisions.choice: who had committed murder: the rebels did, and Barabbas was one of them
decisions.reason: The relative pronoun is plural. Barabbas is counted among the rebels who killed people. Luke 23:19 says he himself was in prison for murder.

decisions.choice: men who had fought against the Romans
decisions.reason: Readable says what the rebels had done. That the uprising was against Rome is clear from the setting, though Mark does not say it.

source.text: καὶ ἀναβὰς ὁ ὄχλος ἤρξατο αἰτεῖσθαι καθὼς ἐποίει αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And having gone up the crowd began to ask [him to do] as he was doing for them.

en.L: And the crowd went up and began to ask [him to do] as he usually did for them.
en.B: The crowd came up and began to ask Pilate to do for them what he always did.
en.R: A crowd came to Pilate. They asked him to set a prisoner free, as he always did.

es.L: Y la multitud subió y comenzó a pedir [que hiciera] según solía hacer con ellos.
es.B: La multitud subió y comenzó a pedirle a Pilato que hiciera por ellos lo que siempre hacía.
es.R: Una multitud llegó adonde estaba Pilato. Le pidieron que soltara a un preso, como hacía siempre.

sw.L: Na umati ukapanda, ukaanza kuomba [awafanyie] kama alivyokuwa akiwafanyia.
sw.B: Umati wa watu ulipanda, ukaanza kumwomba Pilato awafanyie kama alivyokuwa akifanya siku zote.
sw.R: Umati wa watu ulikuja kwa Pilato. Wakamwomba amwachilie huru mfungwa mmoja, kama alivyofanya kila mara.

decisions.choice: having gone up: the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts have a word that sounds alike and means "having shouted". The SBLGNT reads "having gone up", that is, the crowd came up to Pilate's residence, which stood on higher ground. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: as he was doing for them: as was his custom
decisions.reason: This points back to the custom of 15:6.

decisions.choice: the crowd: people who came for the release
decisions.reason: Mark does not say who they were. They had come to ask for the yearly release.

decisions.choice: Pilate (B); to set a prisoner free (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced names Pilate, and Readable says what they asked for.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς λέγων· Θέλετε ἀπολύσω ὑμῖν τὸν βασιλέα τῶν Ἰουδαίων;

records.literal_gloss: But Pilate answered them, saying, Do you want I should release to you the King of the Jews?

en.L: But Pilate answered them, saying, "Do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?"
en.B: Pilate replied, "Shall I set free the King of the Jews for you? Is that what you want?"
en.R: Pilate asked them, "Do you want me to let the king of the Jewish people go free?"

es.L: Pero Pilato les respondió, diciendo: «¿{{plural_you:Quieren|Queréis}} que {{plural_you:les|os}} suelte al Rey de los judíos?».
es.B: Pilato les contestó: «¿{{plural_you:Les|Os}} dejo libre al Rey de los judíos? ¿Es eso lo que {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}}?».
es.R: Pilato les preguntó: «¿{{plural_you:Quieren|Queréis}} que deje en libertad al rey del pueblo judío?».

sw.L: Lakini Pilato akawajibu, akisema, "Mnataka niwafungulie Mfalme wa Wayahudi?"
sw.B: Pilato aliwajibu, "Niwafungulie Mfalme wa Wayahudi? Ndivyo mnavyotaka?"
sw.R: Pilato aliwauliza, "Mnataka nimwachilie huru mfalme wa Wayahudi?"

decisions.choice: answered: replied to their request
decisions.reason: As often in Mark, "answer" means to respond to what was said or done.

decisions.choice: the King of the Jews: Pilate uses the title with scorn
decisions.reason: Pilate takes up the charge (15:2). Spoken by him it mocks the leaders and the prisoner, but Mark's readers know it is truer than Pilate means.

decisions.choice: the king of the Jewish people
decisions.reason: As in 15:2.

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on the verbs and pronouns addressed to the crowd (quieren|queréis, les|os)
decisions.reason: Spanish has two plural forms of "you", Latin American "ustedes" (the default) and Peninsular "vosotros"; the reader setting chooses between them. English has no such choice, so these spans have no English counterpart. The same throughout the chapter.

source.text: ἐγίνωσκεν γὰρ ὅτι διὰ φθόνον παραδεδώκεισαν αὐτὸν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς.

records.literal_gloss: He was knowing for that because of envy had handed over him the chief priests.

en.L: For he knew that it was because of envy that the chief priests had handed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over.
en.B: Pilate could see that envy was what had moved the chief priests to hand {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to him.
en.R: Pilate knew that the leading priests had handed Jesus over to him because they were jealous of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Porque sabía que por envidia {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} habían entregado los jefes de los sacerdotes.
es.B: Pilato se daba cuenta de que los jefes de los sacerdotes se {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} habían entregado por envidia.
es.R: Pilato sabía que los jefes de los sacerdotes le habían entregado a Jesús porque {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} tenían envidia.

sw.L: Kwa maana alijua kwamba kwa sababu ya wivu wakuu wa makuhani walikuwa wamemkabidhi.
sw.B: Pilato aliweza kuona kwamba wakuu wa makuhani walikuwa wamemkabidhi kwake kwa sababu ya wivu.
sw.R: Pilato alijua kwamba wakuu wa makuhani walimkabidhi Yesu kwake kwa sababu walikuwa na wivu juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.

decisions.choice: envy: jealousy of Jesus' standing with the people
alternatives: a just concern for the law
decisions.reason: The word means ill will at another's success. The leaders feared the crowds who listened to Jesus (11:18; 12:12).

decisions.choice: for: Mark explains why Pilate offered to release Jesus
decisions.reason: Pilate hoped the crowd would choose Jesus over the priests' wishes.

decisions.choice: had handed over: the same verb as in 15:1
decisions.reason: Mark keeps returning to the word of the passion predictions.

decisions.choice: to him
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "to him" so it is clear the priests handed Jesus to Pilate. The first "him" is Jesus, the second Pilate.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς ἀνέσεισαν τὸν ὄχλον ἵνα μᾶλλον τὸν Βαραββᾶν ἀπολύσῃ αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: But the chief priests stirred up the crowd that rather Barabbas he should release to them.

en.L: But the chief priests stirred up the crowd [to ask] that he should release Barabbas to them instead.
en.B: But the chief priests worked up the crowd to have him free Barabbas for them instead.
en.R: But the leading priests got the crowd excited. They urged them to ask Pilate to free Barabbas instead of Jesus.

es.L: Pero los jefes de los sacerdotes agitaron a la multitud [para que pidiera] que les soltara más bien a Barrabás.
es.B: Pero los jefes de los sacerdotes incitaron a la multitud a pedir que, en lugar de eso, les soltara a Barrabás.
es.R: Pero los jefes de los sacerdotes alborotaron a la gente. Les dijeron que le pidieran a Pilato que soltara a Barrabás en lugar de Jesús.

sw.L: Lakini wakuu wa makuhani waliuchochea umati [uombe] kwamba awafungulie Baraba badala yake.
sw.B: Lakini wakuu wa makuhani waliuchochea umati ili uombe awafungulie Baraba badala yake.
sw.R: Lakini wakuu wa makuhani waliwachochea watu. Wakawahimiza wamwombe Pilato amwachilie Baraba badala ya Yesu.

decisions.choice: stirred up: shook up, incited
decisions.reason: The verb means to shake. It describes stirring people to action.

decisions.choice: that he should release Barabbas: the purpose of the priests' stirring
alternatives: what the crowd decided by itself
decisions.reason: The clause says what the priests aimed at.

decisions.choice: instead of Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable says whom Barabbas was chosen over.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος πάλιν ἀποκριθεὶς ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Τί οὖν θέλετε ποιήσω ὃν λέγετε τὸν βασιλέα τῶν Ἰουδαίων;

records.literal_gloss: And Pilate again answering was saying to them, What then do you want I should do [with him] whom you call the King of the Jews?

en.L: And Pilate again answered and said to them, "What then do you want me to do [with the one] whom you call the King of the Jews?"
en.B: Pilate spoke to them again. "Then what would you have me do with the man you call the King of the Jews?"
en.R: Pilate asked them again, "Then what should I do with this man? You call {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} the king of the Jews."

es.L: Y Pilato, respondiendo otra vez, les decía: «¿Qué, pues, {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} que haga [con el] que {{plural_you:llaman|llamáis}} el Rey de los judíos?».
es.B: Pilato volvió a hablarles: «Entonces, ¿qué {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} que haga con el que {{plural_you:ustedes llaman|vosotros llamáis}} el Rey de los judíos?».
es.R: Pilato les preguntó otra vez: «Entonces, ¿qué hago con este hombre? {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}} {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} {{plural_you:llaman|llamáis}} el rey del pueblo judío».

sw.L: Naye Pilato, akijibu tena, akawaambia, "Basi mnataka nimfanye nini [yule] mnayemwita Mfalme wa Wayahudi?"
sw.B: Pilato aliwaambia tena, "Basi mnataka nimfanye nini mtu huyu mnayemwita Mfalme wa Wayahudi?"
sw.R: Pilato aliwauliza tena, "Basi nimfanye nini mtu huyu? Ninyi mnamwita mfalme wa Wayahudi."

decisions.choice: what do you want me to do with the one whom you call: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: what shall I do with the King of the Jews (without "do you want" or "whom you call")
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts lack "do you want" and some lack "whom you call". The SBLGNT keeps both. The sense is the same: Pilate puts the title on the crowd's lips. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: whom you call: Pilate distances himself from the title
decisions.reason: Pilate says it is their name for him, not his.

decisions.choice: then: since you want Barabbas
decisions.reason: The small word draws a conclusion from their request.

decisions.choice: Then what should I do with this man? You call him the king of the Jews.
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the question into two short sentences.

source.text: οἱ δὲ πάλιν ἔκραξαν· Σταύρωσον αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And again they cried out, Crucify him.

en.L: And they cried out again, "Crucify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"
en.B: They shouted back, "Crucify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"
en.R: The people shouted, "Nail {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to a cross!"

es.L: Y ellos gritaron otra vez: «¡Crucifícalo!».
es.B: Ellos respondieron a gritos: «¡Crucifícalo!».
es.R: La gente gritó: «¡Clávalo en una cruz!».

sw.L: Nao wakapiga kelele tena, "Msulubishe!"
sw.B: Walijibu kwa kelele, "Msulubishe!"
sw.R: Watu walipiga kelele, "Mpigilie misumari msalabani!"

decisions.choice: again: in reply, once more
alternatives: a second time they said this
decisions.reason: The crowd has not yet called for crucifixion. The word here means back, in answer, or it looks back to their shouting for Barabbas.

decisions.choice: crucify: the Roman death for slaves and rebels
decisions.reason: The condemned man was fastened to a wooden cross and left to die. It was meant to shame and to warn.

decisions.choice: Nail him to a cross
decisions.reason: Readable explains what crucifixion was. Nails are attested for crucifixion, and the risen Jesus shows his hands (Luke 24:39; John 20:25).

source.text: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Τί γὰρ ἐποίησεν κακόν;

records.literal_gloss: And Pilate was saying to them, What for did he do evil?

en.L: And Pilate said to them, "Why, what evil has {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} done?"
en.B: Pilate asked them, "Why? What crime has {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} committed?"
en.R: Pilate asked, "Why? What wrong has {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} done?"

es.L: Y Pilato les decía: «Pues ¿qué mal ha hecho?».
es.B: Pilato les preguntó: «¿Por qué? ¿Qué delito ha cometido?».
es.R: Pilato preguntó: «¿Por qué? ¿Qué cosa mala ha hecho?».

sw.L: Naye Pilato akawaambia, "Kwani amefanya ubaya gani?"
sw.B: Pilato aliwauliza, "Kwa nini? Amefanya kosa gani?"
sw.R: Pilato aliuliza, "Kwa nini? Amefanya baya gani?"

decisions.choice: What for: why, with surprise
decisions.reason: The small word adds force to the question: why, what has he done?

decisions.choice: evil: wrongdoing, a crime
decisions.reason: Pilate asks what crime would deserve death.

decisions.choice: crime
decisions.reason: In a court the question is about a crime.

source.text: οἱ δὲ περισσῶς ἔκραξαν· Σταύρωσον αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: But all the more they cried out, Crucify him.

en.L: But they cried out all the more, "Crucify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"
en.B: But they only shouted louder, "Crucify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"
en.R: But they shouted even louder, "Nail {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to a cross!"

es.L: Pero ellos gritaron aún más: «¡Crucifícalo!».
es.B: Pero ellos solo gritaron más fuerte: «¡Crucifícalo!».
es.R: Pero ellos gritaron todavía más fuerte: «¡Clávalo en una cruz!».

sw.L: Lakini wao wakapiga kelele zaidi sana, "Msulubishe!"
sw.B: Lakini wao walizidi kupiga kelele, "Msulubishe!"
sw.R: Lakini walipiga kelele kwa sauti kubwa zaidi, "Mpigilie misumari msalabani!"

decisions.choice: all the more: louder and harder
decisions.reason: The crowd does not answer Pilate's question. They only shout more.

decisions.choice: cried out: the same verb as in 15:13
decisions.reason: Mark repeats the verb and the shout.

decisions.choice: Nail him to a cross
decisions.reason: As in 15:13.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος βουλόμενος τῷ ὄχλῳ τὸ ἱκανὸν ποιῆσαι ἀπέλυσεν αὐτοῖς τὸν Βαραββᾶν, καὶ παρέδωκεν τὸν Ἰησοῦν φραγελλώσας ἵνα σταυρωθῇ.

records.literal_gloss: And Pilate wanting the crowd the satisfactory to do released to them Barabbas, and handed over Jesus, having flogged [him], that he might be crucified.

en.L: And Pilate, wanting to satisfy the crowd, released Barabbas to them, and having flogged Jesus, he handed [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] over to be crucified.
en.B: So Pilate, wishing to please the crowd, freed Barabbas for them. He had Jesus flogged and then handed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over for crucifixion.
en.R: Pilate wanted to keep the crowd happy. So he set Barabbas free. He had Jesus beaten with whips. Then he handed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to be killed on a cross.

es.L: Y Pilato, queriendo satisfacer a la multitud, les soltó a Barrabás, y, después de azotar a Jesús, [{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}] entregó para que fuera crucificado.
es.B: Así que Pilato, queriendo complacer a la multitud, les dejó libre a Barrabás. Mandó azotar a Jesús, y luego {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} entregó para que fuera crucificado.
es.R: Pilato quería tener contenta a la gente. Por eso soltó a Barrabás. Mandó que azotaran a Jesús con látigos. Después {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} entregó para que lo mataran en una cruz.

sw.L: Naye Pilato, akitaka kuuridhisha umati, aliwafungulia Baraba, na akiisha kumpiga Yesu mijeledi, akamkabidhi ili asulubiwe.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo Pilato, akitaka kuuridhisha umati, aliwafungulia Baraba. Akaamuru Yesu apigwe mijeledi, kisha akamkabidhi ili asulubiwe.
sw.R: Pilato alitaka kuwafurahisha watu. Kwa hiyo alimwachilia Baraba. Akaagiza Yesu achapwe viboko. Kisha akamkabidhi ili auawe msalabani.

decisions.choice: to do the satisfactory to the crowd: to satisfy them
decisions.reason: The phrase is a Latin way of speaking put into Greek: to do enough for someone, to please them.

decisions.choice: flogged: scourged with a Roman whip
decisions.reason: The whip had pieces of bone or metal in its leather straps. Scourging came before crucifixion and could kill a man by itself.

decisions.choice: having flogged: Pilate's soldiers did it at his order
alternatives: Pilate did it with his own hands
decisions.reason: As often, the one who gives the order is said to do the act.

decisions.choice: handed over: the passion prediction fulfilled
decisions.reason: Jesus said the Gentiles would mock him, spit on him, flog him and kill him (10:34). Mark uses the same word for flogging.

decisions.choice: had Jesus flogged (B); had Jesus beaten with whips (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that Pilate gave the order. Readable says what flogging was.

source.text: Οἱ δὲ στρατιῶται ἀπήγαγον αὐτὸν ἔσω τῆς αὐλῆς, ὅ ἐστιν πραιτώριον, καὶ συγκαλοῦσιν ὅλην τὴν σπεῖραν.

records.literal_gloss: And the soldiers led away him inside the courtyard, which is [the] praetorium, and they call together all the cohort.

en.L: And the soldiers led {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} away inside the courtyard, that is, [the] praetorium, and they call together the whole cohort.
en.B: The soldiers took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} into the palace courtyard, that is, the governor's headquarters, and called the whole company of soldiers together.
en.R: The soldiers took Jesus into the courtyard of the governor's palace. They called all the other soldiers of their unit together.

es.L: Y los soldados {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llevaron dentro del patio, que es [el] pretorio, y convocan a toda la cohorte.
es.B: Los soldados {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llevaron al patio del palacio, es decir, a la residencia del gobernador, y reunieron a toda la cohorte.
es.R: Los soldados llevaron a Jesús al patio del palacio del gobernador. Llamaron a todos los demás soldados de su tropa.

sw.L: Na askari walimpeleka ndani ya ua, yaani ikulu, nao wanakusanya kikosi kizima.
sw.B: Askari walimpeleka ndani ya ua wa jumba, yaani ikulu ya mkuu wa mkoa, wakakusanya kikosi kizima cha askari.
sw.R: Askari walimpeleka Yesu ndani ya ua wa ikulu ya mkuu wa mkoa. Wakawaita askari wengine wote wa kikosi chao.

decisions.choice: courtyard: the court of the palace
decisions.reason: The word means an enclosed court and can stand for the palace around it, as in 14:54.

decisions.choice: praetorium: the governor's residence
decisions.reason: The Latin word was used for a commander's or governor's headquarters. In Jerusalem it was probably Herod's former palace, or else the Antonia fortress beside the temple.

decisions.choice: cohort: a unit of Roman soldiers, up to several hundred men
decisions.reason: A full cohort had about six hundred men. Mark likely means all the soldiers on duty there.

decisions.choice: they call together: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: Mark tells the scene vividly in the present tense; the sense is past.

decisions.choice: the governor's headquarters; the whole company of soldiers (B); soldiers of their unit (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Latin terms. Balanced and Readable say what they were.

decisions.choice: pretorio (L), la residencia del gobernador (B), el palacio del gobernador (R); cohorte (L, B), los soldados de su tropa (R)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 27:27: Literal keeps the Latin word, Balanced says what the building was (meaning decision m2, uncertain), and Readable uses everyday words. "Cohorte" is the Roman unit itself (meaning decision m3), still understood in Spanish.

decisions.choice: ikulu (praetorium); kikosi (cohort); mkuu wa mkoa (governor)
decisions.reason: The words used for the same place and unit in Matthew 27:27 and John 18:28 (meaning decisions m2, m3). "Ikulu" is the official residence of a ruler, which is what the praetorium most likely was.

source.text: καὶ ἐνδιδύσκουσιν αὐτὸν πορφύραν καὶ περιτιθέασιν αὐτῷ πλέξαντες ἀκάνθινον στέφανον·

records.literal_gloss: And they clothe him [in] purple, and they put on him having woven a thorny crown.

en.L: And they clothe {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [in] purple, and having woven a crown of thorns, they put [it] on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: They put a purple robe on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, wove a crown out of thorny branches and put it on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head.
en.R: They put a purple robe on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, the color worn by kings. They twisted thorny branches into a crown and put it on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} visten de púrpura, y, habiendo trenzado una corona de espinas, [la] ponen sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Entonces {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vistieron con un manto de púrpura, trenzaron una corona con ramas espinosas y se la pusieron en la cabeza.
es.R: Luego {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pusieron un manto de color púrpura, el color que usaban los reyes. Torcieron unas ramas con espinas para hacer una corona y se la pusieron en la cabeza.

sw.L: Nao wanamvika [vazi la] zambarau, na wakiisha kusuka taji ya miiba, wanamwekea.
sw.B: Walimvika joho la zambarau, wakasuka taji kwa matawi yenye miiba, wakaiweka juu ya kichwa {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}.
sw.R: Walimvika vazi la zambarau, rangi ambayo wafalme walivaa. Wakasokota matawi yenye miiba kuwa taji, wakaiweka juu ya kichwa {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}.

decisions.choice: purple: a royal color
decisions.reason: Purple dye was costly and was worn by kings. The soldiers may have used a faded red military cloak (Matthew 27:28) to look like a king's robe.

decisions.choice: a crown of thorns: a mock king's wreath
decisions.reason: Rulers wore wreaths. The soldiers made one of thorny branches to mock Jesus as king. It also caused him pain.

decisions.choice: they clothe, they put on: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: As in 15:16, the sense is past.

decisions.choice: the color worn by kings
decisions.reason: Readable explains why purple was used.

source.text: καὶ ἤρξαντο ἀσπάζεσθαι αὐτόν· Χαῖρε, βασιλεῦ τῶν Ἰουδαίων·

records.literal_gloss: and they began to greet him, Hail, King of the Jews.

en.L: and they began to salute {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Hail, King of the Jews!"
en.B: Then they started saluting {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: "Long live the King of the Jews!"
en.R: Then they began to bow and call out to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Long live the king of the Jews!"

es.L: y comenzaron a saludarlo: «¡Salve, Rey de los judíos!».
es.B: Luego empezaron a saludarlo: «¡Viva el Rey de los judíos!».
es.R: Después empezaron a inclinarse ante {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y a gritarle: «¡Viva el rey de los judíos!».

sw.L: na wakaanza kumsalimu, "Salamu, Mfalme wa Wayahudi!"
sw.B: Kisha wakaanza kumsalimu, "Uishi milele, Mfalme wa Wayahudi!"
sw.R: Kisha wakaanza kumwinamia na kumwita kwa sauti, "Uishi milele, mfalme wa Wayahudi!"

decisions.choice: Hail: the greeting given to an emperor
decisions.reason: Soldiers greeted the emperor with "Hail, Caesar". They mock Jesus with the same form.

decisions.choice: to salute: to greet with respect
decisions.reason: The verb means to greet. Here it is a mocking salute.

decisions.choice: Long live
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a cheer for a ruler that is still in use. Literal keeps the traditional "Hail".

decisions.choice: ¡Salve...! (L); ¡Viva...! (B, R)
decisions.reason: The greeting given to an emperor (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps "salve", the old salute to a ruler, as in John 19:3; Balanced and Readable use the cry with which people acclaim a king, as the English "Long live" does.

decisions.choice: "Salamu" (L); "Uishi milele" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The greeting given to an emperor (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the plain greeting, as in John 19:3; Balanced and Readable follow the English "Long live" with "uishi milele", the acclamation of a king, so the mock homage is heard.

source.text: καὶ ἔτυπτον αὐτοῦ τὴν κεφαλὴν καλάμῳ καὶ ἐνέπτυον αὐτῷ, καὶ τιθέντες τὰ γόνατα προσεκύνουν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And they were striking his head with a reed and were spitting on him, and bending the knees were bowing down to him.

en.L: And they kept striking {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} head with a reed and spitting on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and bending [their] knees, they were bowing down to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Again and again they hit {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on the head with a stick, spat on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and went down on their knees to pay {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} homage.
en.R: They kept hitting {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on the head with a stick and spitting on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They got down on their knees in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as if {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} were a king.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} golpeaban la cabeza con una caña y escupían sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y, doblando las rodillas, se postraban ante {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Una y otra vez {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pegaban en la cabeza con una vara, escupían sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y se arrodillaban ante {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} para rendirle homenaje.
es.R: No dejaban de golpearle la cabeza con una vara y de escupir sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Se ponían de rodillas delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, como si fuera un rey.

sw.L: Na walikuwa wakimpiga kichwa {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}} kwa mwanzi na kumtemea mate, na wakipiga magoti walikuwa wakimsujudia.
sw.B: Wakampiga kichwani kwa fimbo tena na tena, wakamtemea mate, wakapiga magoti mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kumpa heshima.
sw.R: Waliendelea kumpiga kichwani kwa fimbo na kumtemea mate. Walipiga magoti mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kana kwamba ni mfalme.

decisions.choice: a reed: a stick or cane
decisions.reason: The reed may have been given him as a mock scepter (Matthew 27:29) before they hit him with it.

decisions.choice: bowing down to: paying homage, kneeling before
decisions.reason: The verb is used for bowing before a king or for worship. Here it is mocking homage.

decisions.choice: were striking, were spitting, were bowing: repeated actions
decisions.reason: The tenses show the soldiers doing these things again and again.

decisions.choice: spitting on him: as Jesus said and as the servant of Isaiah suffered
decisions.reason: Jesus said the Gentiles would spit on him (10:34). Isaiah 50:6 speaks of one who did not hide his face from spitting.

decisions.choice: as if he were a king
decisions.reason: Readable makes the mockery clear.

decisions.choice: caña (L); vara (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek names a reed stalk, which Literal keeps (meaning decision m1). Balanced and Readable say "vara", a stick, as the English does and as in Matthew 27:29-30.

decisions.choice: mwanzi (L); fimbo (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek names a reed stalk, which Literal keeps (meaning decision m1). Balanced and Readable say "fimbo" (a stick), as the English does and as in Matthew 27:29-30.

source.text: καὶ ὅτε ἐνέπαιξαν αὐτῷ, ἐξέδυσαν αὐτὸν τὴν πορφύραν καὶ ἐνέδυσαν αὐτὸν τὰ ἱμάτια τὰ ἴδια.

records.literal_gloss: And when they had mocked him, they took off him the purple and put on him the garments his own.

en.L: And when they had mocked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they took the purple off {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own garments on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: When they had finished mocking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they stripped the purple robe off {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and dressed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own clothes.
en.R: When the soldiers were done making fun of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they took off the purple robe. They put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own clothes back on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y cuando se hubieron burlado de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} quitaron la púrpura y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} pusieron {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} propias ropas.
es.B: Cuando terminaron de burlarse de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} quitaron el manto de púrpura y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vistieron con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propia ropa.
es.R: Cuando los soldados terminaron de reírse de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} quitaron el manto de púrpura. Luego {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} volvieron a poner {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propia ropa.

sw.L: Na walipokwisha kumdhihaki, walimvua ile zambarau, wakamvika mavazi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} mwenyewe.
sw.B: Walipomaliza kumdhihaki, walimvua lile joho la zambarau, wakamvika nguo {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} mwenyewe.
sw.R: Askari walipomaliza kumcheka, walimvua lile vazi la zambarau. Wakamvika tena nguo {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} mwenyewe.

decisions.choice: mocked: the passion prediction fulfilled
decisions.reason: Jesus said the Gentiles would mock him (10:34). Mark uses the same verb.

decisions.choice: garments: his outer clothes
decisions.reason: The word means clothing, especially the outer robe. These are divided in 15:24.

decisions.choice: the purple robe
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply the noun Greek leaves implied.

source.text: καὶ ἐξάγουσιν αὐτὸν ἵνα σταυρώσωσιν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And they lead out him that they might crucify him.

en.L: And they lead {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} out to crucify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Then they took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} out to crucify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Then they led {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} out of the city to kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} on a cross.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} sacan para crucificarlo.
es.B: Luego {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} sacaron para crucificarlo.
es.R: Después {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llevaron fuera de la ciudad para matarlo en una cruz.

sw.L: Nao wanamtoa nje ili wamsulubishe.
sw.B: Kisha wakamtoa nje ili wakamsulubishe.
sw.R: Kisha wakamchukua nje ya mji ili wakamuue msalabani.

decisions.choice: they lead out: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: As often in Mark, the sense is past.

decisions.choice: led out: outside the city
decisions.reason: Executions took place outside the city walls (Hebrews 13:12).

decisions.choice: out of the city
decisions.reason: Readable says where they took him; Hebrews 13:12 says Jesus suffered outside the gate.

source.text: Καὶ ἀγγαρεύουσιν παράγοντά τινα Σίμωνα Κυρηναῖον ἐρχόμενον ἀπ’ ἀγροῦ, τὸν πατέρα Ἀλεξάνδρου καὶ Ῥούφου, ἵνα ἄρῃ τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And they compel passing by someone Simon a Cyrenian coming from [the] country, the father of Alexander and Rufus, that he might carry the cross of him.

en.L: And they compel a certain passerby, Simon, a Cyrenian, coming from [the] country, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to carry {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} cross.
en.B: A man named Simon from Cyrene was coming in from the countryside and passing by; he was the father of Alexander and Rufus. The soldiers pressed him into carrying the cross for Jesus.
en.R: A man named Simon was walking by, coming into the city from the fields. He was from Cyrene in North Africa, and he was the father of Alexander and Rufus. The soldiers made him carry Jesus' cross.

es.L: Y obligan a uno que pasaba, a un tal Simón, cireneo, que venía del campo, el padre de Alejandro y de Rufo, a que cargara {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} cruz.
es.B: Un hombre de Cirene llamado Simón, padre de Alejandro y de Rufo, pasaba por allí al volver del campo. Los soldados lo obligaron a cargar la cruz de Jesús.
es.R: Un hombre llamado Simón pasaba por allí. Venía del campo y entraba en la ciudad. Era de Cirene, en el norte de África, y era el padre de Alejandro y de Rufo. Los soldados lo obligaron a cargar la cruz de Jesús.

sw.L: Nao wanamlazimisha mtu mmoja aliyekuwa akipita, Simoni Mkirene, akitoka shambani, baba yao Aleksanda na Rufo, aubebe msalaba {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.B: Mtu mmoja wa Kirene aitwaye Simoni, baba yao Aleksanda na Rufo, alikuwa akipita pale akitoka shambani. Askari wakamlazimisha aubebe msalaba wa Yesu.
sw.R: Mtu mmoja aitwaye Simoni alikuwa akipita pale. Alikuwa akitoka mashambani, akiingia mjini. Alikuwa wa mji wa Kirene, kaskazini mwa Afrika, na alikuwa baba yao Aleksanda na Rufo. Askari walimlazimisha aubebe msalaba wa Yesu.

decisions.choice: compel: force into service, as Roman soldiers could
decisions.reason: Roman soldiers had the right to make a civilian carry a load for them. Jesus speaks of this in Matthew 5:41.

decisions.choice: Cyrenian: from Cyrene, a city in North Africa with a large Jewish community
decisions.reason: Jews from Cyrene had their own synagogue in Jerusalem (Acts 6:9). Simon may have come for Passover or lived in the area.

decisions.choice: the father of Alexander and Rufus: men Mark's readers knew
decisions.reason: Mark names the sons as if his readers knew them. A Rufus in the church at Rome is greeted in Romans 16:13; he may be the same man, but that cannot be shown.

decisions.choice: the cross: the crossbeam carried by the condemned man
decisions.reason: The condemned man usually carried the crossbeam to the place of execution. Jesus, weakened by the flogging, could not.

decisions.choice: they compel: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: The sense is past.

decisions.choice: The soldiers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject. Readable also says where Cyrene was.

source.text: καὶ φέρουσιν αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸν Γολγοθᾶν τόπον, ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον Κρανίου Τόπος.

records.literal_gloss: And they bring him to the Golgotha place, which is being translated, Of a Skull Place.

en.L: And they bring {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to the place Golgotha, which is translated, Place of a Skull.
en.B: They brought Jesus to a place named Golgotha, meaning Place of a Skull.
en.R: They took Jesus to a place called Golgotha. That name means "the Place of the Skull."

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llevan al lugar Gólgota, que traducido es Lugar de la Calavera.
es.B: Llevaron a Jesús a un lugar llamado Gólgota, que significa Lugar de la Calavera.
es.R: Llevaron a Jesús a un lugar llamado Gólgota. Ese nombre quiere decir «el Lugar de la Calavera».

sw.L: Nao wanampeleka mahali pa Golgotha, maana yake ikitafsiriwa ni Mahali pa Fuvu.
sw.B: Walimpeleka Yesu mahali panapoitwa Golgotha, maana yake Mahali pa Fuvu.
sw.R: Walimpeleka Yesu mahali panapoitwa Golgotha. Jina hilo maana yake ni "Mahali pa Fuvu."

decisions.choice: Golgotha: an Aramaic word for skull
decisions.reason: Mark gives the Aramaic name and then its meaning, as he does with other Aramaic words (5:41; 7:34).

decisions.choice: Place of a Skull: why it had this name is not known
decisions.reason: The name may come from the shape of the hill or rock, or from its use for executions. The Gospels place it outside the city near a road (15:29; John 19:20).

decisions.choice: they bring: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: The sense is past.

decisions.choice: That name means
decisions.reason: Readable makes a new sentence for Mark's explanation.

decisions.choice: Gólgota ... Lugar de la Calavera (every level)
decisions.reason: Mark translates the name (meaning decision m1), so each level gives the local name and its meaning, as in Matthew 27:33 and John 19:17. "Calvario" comes from the Latin and is not in the Greek.

decisions.choice: Golgotha ... Mahali pa Fuvu (every level)
decisions.reason: Mark translates the name (meaning decision m1), so each level gives the local name and its meaning, as in Matthew 27:33 and John 19:17. "Kalvari" comes from the Latin and is not in the Greek.

source.text: καὶ ἐδίδουν αὐτῷ ἐσμυρνισμένον οἶνον, ὃς δὲ οὐκ ἔλαβεν.

records.literal_gloss: And they were giving him having been mixed with myrrh wine; but he not took.

en.L: And they were offering {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} wine mixed with myrrh, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not take [it].
en.B: They tried to give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} wine flavored with myrrh, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would not take it.
en.R: They offered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} wine mixed with myrrh, a bitter spice. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would not drink it.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} daban vino mezclado con mirra; pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no [lo] tomó.
es.B: Intentaron darle vino mezclado con mirra, pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no lo quiso tomar.
es.R: Allí {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} ofrecieron vino mezclado con mirra, una especia amarga. Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no quiso beberlo.

sw.L: Nao walikuwa wakimpa divai iliyochanganywa na manemane; lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hakuipokea.
sw.B: Walijaribu kumpa divai iliyochanganywa na manemane, lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hakuikubali.
sw.R: Walimpa divai iliyochanganywa na manemane, kiungo kichungu. Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hakutaka kuinywa.

decisions.choice: wine mixed with myrrh: perhaps a drink to dull the pain
alternatives: a drink meant to mock him
a costly wine given as an honor
decisions.reason: Proverbs 31:6 says to give strong drink to one who is perishing, and Jewish tradition tells of women in Jerusalem who gave a drugged drink to the condemned. Myrrh also flavored fine wine. Mark does not say why it was given.

decisions.choice: were offering: they tried to give
decisions.reason: The tense shows an attempt. He refused.

decisions.choice: he did not take it: Jesus refuses what would dull his suffering
decisions.reason: At the last supper Jesus said he would not drink wine again until the kingdom of God (14:25). He also goes to death fully aware.

decisions.choice: a bitter spice
decisions.reason: Readable says what myrrh was.

source.text: καὶ σταυροῦσιν αὐτὸν καὶ διαμερίζονται τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ, βάλλοντες κλῆρον ἐπ’ αὐτὰ τίς τί ἄρῃ.

records.literal_gloss: And they crucify him and they divide the garments of him, casting a lot for them, who what should take.

en.L: And they crucify {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and divide {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} garments, casting lots for them [to see] who should take what.
en.B: Then they crucified {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They shared out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clothes by throwing dice for them to see what each would get.
en.R: Then the soldiers nailed Jesus to the cross. They divided {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clothes among themselves. They threw dice to decide who would get each piece.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} crucifican y se reparten {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} ropas, echando suertes sobre ellas [para ver] qué se llevaría cada uno.
es.B: Entonces {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} crucificaron. Se repartieron {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ropa echando suertes para ver qué le tocaba a cada uno.
es.R: Luego los soldados clavaron a Jesús en la cruz. Se repartieron {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ropa. Echaron los dados para decidir qué prenda se llevaría cada uno.

sw.L: Nao wanamsulubisha, na wanagawana mavazi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, wakiyatupia kura [kuona] nani achukue nini.
sw.B: Kisha walimsulubisha. Wakagawana nguo {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} kwa kuzitupia kura ili kuona kila mmoja atapata nini.
sw.R: Kisha askari walimpigilia Yesu misumari msalabani. Wakagawana nguo {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}. Waliamua kwa bahati ni nani atachukua kila nguo.

decisions.choice: they divide his garments, casting lots: Psalm 22:19
decisions.reason: The psalm says: they divide my garments among them, and for my clothing they cast lots. Mark uses the psalm's words without saying he quotes it.

decisions.choice: casting lots: throwing marked stones or dice to decide
decisions.reason: Lots were small objects thrown to make a choice by chance.

decisions.choice: dividing the garments: the executioners kept the clothes of the condemned
decisions.reason: The condemned were crucified naked or nearly so, and their clothes went to the soldiers.

decisions.choice: they crucify, they divide: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: Mark tells the crucifixion itself in a few plain words. The sense is past.

decisions.choice: throwing dice (B); threw dice (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a familiar game of chance for lots.

decisions.choice: echando suertes (L, B); echaron los dados (R)
alternatives: echando los dados (B, as the English "throwing dice")
decisions.reason: Lots let chance decide who got each garment (meaning decision m2). "Echar suertes" is the Spanish phrase for it and keeps the link with Psalm 22 (meaning decision m1), as in Matthew 27:35; Readable names the dice, as the English does.

decisions.choice: kutupia kura (L, B); kuamua kwa bahati (R)
alternatives: kutupa dadu (R, as the English "threw dice")
decisions.reason: Lots let chance decide who got each garment (meaning decision m2). "Kupiga kura" today usually means to vote, so Literal and Balanced say "kutupia kura" and Readable "decide by chance", as in Matthew 27:35 and John 19:24.

source.text: Ἦν δὲ ὥρα τρίτη καὶ ἐσταύρωσαν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Now it was [the] hour third and they crucified him.

en.L: Now it was the third hour, and they crucified {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: It was nine in the morning when they crucified {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: It was about nine o'clock in the morning when they nailed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to the cross.

es.L: Y era la hora tercera, y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} crucificaron.
es.B: Eran las nueve de la mañana cuando {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} crucificaron.
es.R: Eran como las nueve de la mañana cuando {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} clavaron en la cruz.

sw.L: Basi ilikuwa saa tatu, nao wakamsulubisha.
sw.B: Ilikuwa saa tatu asubuhi walipomsulubisha.
sw.R: Ilikuwa yapata saa tatu asubuhi walipompigilia misumari msalabani.

decisions.choice: the third hour: about nine in the morning
decisions.reason: Jews and Romans counted the hours of daylight from sunrise, about six in the morning. The third hour was about nine. Mark marks the day in three-hour steps: the third, sixth and ninth hours (15:33-34).

decisions.choice: the third hour: the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts read "sixth", making Mark agree with John 19:14, where Jesus is still before Pilate at about the sixth hour. The SBLGNT reads "third". Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: and: when, the time when they crucified him
decisions.reason: The "and" links the time with the event: it was the third hour when they crucified him.

decisions.choice: nine in the morning (B); about nine o'clock in the morning (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the ancient way of counting the hours. Balanced and Readable give the time as we count it, since the third hour after sunrise was about nine o'clock.

decisions.choice: saa tatu at every level; asubuhi added at Balanced and Readable
alternatives: saa tisa (the English "nine in the morning")
decisions.reason: The Greek counts the hours from sunrise, as Swahili time does, so "the third hour" is "saa tatu" with no conversion (meaning decision m1). The same for "saa sita" and "saa tisa" in verses 33 and 34.

source.text: καὶ ἦν ἡ ἐπιγραφὴ τῆς αἰτίας αὐτοῦ ἐπιγεγραμμένη· Ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων.

records.literal_gloss: And there was the inscription of the charge of him having been inscribed, The King of the Jews.

en.L: And the inscription of the charge against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} was inscribed: "The King of the Jews."
en.B: The written charge against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} said, "The King of the Jews."
en.R: A sign was put up that told why {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was being killed. It said, "The King of the Jews."

es.L: Y la inscripción de la acusación contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} estaba escrita: «El Rey de los judíos».
es.B: El letrero con el cargo contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} decía: «El Rey de los judíos».
es.R: Pusieron un letrero que decía por qué {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} mataban. Decía: «El Rey de los judíos».

sw.L: Na maandishi ya shtaka dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} yalikuwa yameandikwa: "Mfalme wa Wayahudi."
sw.B: Maandishi ya shtaka dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} yalisema, "Mfalme wa Wayahudi."
sw.R: Waliweka kibao kilichoeleza kwa nini alikuwa akiuawa. Kiliandikwa, "Mfalme wa Wayahudi."

decisions.choice: the inscription of the charge: a notice giving the crime
decisions.reason: The Romans made the reason for an execution known, on a board carried before the man or fixed to the cross.

decisions.choice: The King of the Jews: the charge on which Jesus died
decisions.reason: It was meant as mockery and as a warning, but for Mark it states the truth about Jesus in the mouth of his enemies.

decisions.choice: a sign that told why he was being killed
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the notice was.

source.text: καὶ σὺν αὐτῷ σταυροῦσιν δύο λῃστάς, ἕνα ἐκ δεξιῶν καὶ ἕνα ἐξ εὐωνύμων αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And with him they crucify two bandits, one at [the] right and one at [the] left of him.

en.L: And with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} they crucify two bandits, one on [the] right and one on [the] left of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: They also crucified two bandits with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, one at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right and one at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} left.
en.R: Two robbers were also nailed to crosses next to Jesus, one on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right side and one on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} left.

es.L: Y con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} crucifican a dos bandidos, uno a [la] derecha y uno a [la] izquierda de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} crucificaron también a dos bandidos, uno a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} derecha y otro a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} izquierda.
es.R: También clavaron en cruces a dos ladrones junto a Jesús, uno a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} derecha y otro a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} izquierda.

sw.L: Na pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} wanawasulubisha majambazi wawili, mmoja upande wa kulia na mmoja upande wa kushoto {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.B: Pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} walisulubisha pia majambazi wawili, mmoja upande wa kulia {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} na mwingine upande wa kushoto {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.R: Majambazi wawili pia walipigiliwa misumari kwenye misalaba karibu na Yesu, mmoja upande wa kulia {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} na mwingine upande wa kushoto {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.

decisions.choice: bandits: armed robbers, a word also used for rebels
decisions.reason: The word means a violent robber. Roman and Jewish writers also used it for those who took up arms against Rome, like the rebels of 15:7. Jesus used it in 14:48.

decisions.choice: one on the right and one on the left: the places James and John asked for
decisions.reason: James and John asked to sit at Jesus' right and left in his glory (10:37, 40). Mark uses the same phrase here.

decisions.choice: the SBLGNT has no verse 28
alternatives: add verse 28: And the Scripture was fulfilled that says, And he was counted with the lawless
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add here: "And the Scripture was fulfilled that says, And he was counted with the lawless." The words come from Isaiah 53:12, which Jesus quotes in Luke 22:37. The earliest manuscripts lack the verse, and Mark rarely quotes Scripture this way himself, so it is likely a later addition taken from Luke. Verse 28 is skipped in the numbering for this reason. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: they crucify: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: The sense is past.

decisions.choice: robbers
decisions.reason: Readable uses the common word. Literal and Balanced keep "bandits", which leaves room for the sense of armed rebels.

decisions.choice: majambazi
decisions.reason: The word is an armed robber, and was also used for rebels against Rome (meaning decision m1). "Jambazi" is the term set for these drafts: a violent robber, not a sneak thief ("mwizi").

source.text: Καὶ οἱ παραπορευόμενοι ἐβλασφήμουν αὐτὸν κινοῦντες τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν καὶ λέγοντες· Οὐὰ ὁ καταλύων τὸν ναὸν καὶ οἰκοδομῶν ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις, σῶσον σεαυτὸν καταβὰς ἀπὸ τοῦ σταυροῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And those passing by were blaspheming him, shaking the heads of them and saying, Aha, the [one] destroying the temple and building [it] in three days, \v 30 save yourself, having come down from the cross.

en.L: And those passing by were blaspheming {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, shaking their heads and saying, "Aha! You who destroy the temple and build [it] in three days, \v 30 save {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} by coming down from the cross!"
en.B: People who went by hurled insults at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, wagging their heads. "Ha!" they said. "So {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} were going to tear down the temple and raise it again in three days! \v 30 Then save {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} by coming down from the cross!"
en.R: People walking by shook their heads and shouted insults at {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They said, "Look at {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}! You said {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} would destroy the temple and build it again in three days. \v 30 So save {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}! Come down from the cross!"

es.L: Y los que pasaban {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} injuriaban, meneando sus cabezas y diciendo: «¡Ajá! Tú que destruyes el templo y [lo] edificas en tres días, \v 30 ¡sálvate a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} mismo bajando de la cruz!».
es.B: La gente que pasaba {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} insultaba y meneaba la cabeza. «¡Ja!», decían. «¡Así que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} ibas a derribar el templo y a reconstruirlo en tres días! \v 30 ¡Pues sálvate a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} mismo bajando de la cruz!».
es.R: La gente que pasaba por allí meneaba la cabeza y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} insultaba a gritos. Decían: «¡Mírate! Decías que ibas a destruir el templo y a construirlo otra vez en tres días. \v 30 ¡Pues sálvate a {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} mismo! ¡Baja de la cruz!».

sw.L: Na wale waliokuwa wakipita walimtukana, wakitikisa vichwa vyao na kusema, "Aha! Wewe unayelibomoa hekalu na kulijenga katika siku tatu, \v 30 jiokoe {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} kwa kushuka kutoka msalabani!"
sw.B: Watu waliokuwa wakipita walimtukana, wakitikisa vichwa vyao. Wakasema, "Aha! Ati {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ndiwe uliyetaka kulibomoa hekalu na kulijenga upya kwa siku tatu! \v 30 Basi jiokoe {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} kwa kushuka kutoka msalabani!"
sw.R: Watu waliopita pale walitikisa vichwa vyao, wakamtukana kwa sauti. Walisema, "Jitazame! Ulisema utalibomoa hekalu na kulijenga upya kwa siku tatu. \v 30 Basi jiokoe {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}! Shuka kutoka msalabani!"

decisions.choice: blaspheming: speaking abuse against him
decisions.reason: The verb means to slander or insult. Mark's readers would also hear in it the charge of blasphemy brought against Jesus (14:64), now turned on those who mock him.

decisions.choice: shaking their heads: Psalm 22:8
decisions.reason: The psalm says: all who see me mock me; they shake their heads. In Lamentations 2:15 passers-by wag their heads at Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: destroying the temple and building it in three days: the charge at the hearing
decisions.reason: False witnesses claimed Jesus said he would destroy the temple and build another in three days (14:58). Mark has not recorded such a saying from Jesus, though he foretold the temple's fall (13:2).

decisions.choice: Aha: a cry of scorn
decisions.reason: The word mocks someone in his downfall.

decisions.choice: save yourself: the mockers' demand, which Jesus refuses
decisions.reason: Jesus had said that whoever wants to save his life will lose it (8:35). He does not come down.

decisions.choice: the taunt split into exclamations
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break the long taunt into shorter cries. Readable says "You said you would" for the participles.

decisions.choice: yourself
decisions.reason: The mockers speak to Jesus, so the pronoun for him is written as a pronoun for Christ.

decisions.choice: ¡Ajá! (L); ¡Ja! (B)
decisions.reason: A cry of scorn (meaning decision m4). "¡Ay!" is the word these drafts use for "woe" and would sound like pity or pain, so Spanish uses the mocking "¡Ajá!" and "¡Ja!". Readable turns it into "¡Mírate!", as the English "Look at you!".

decisions.choice: Aha! (L, B); Ati (B)
decisions.reason: A cry of scorn (meaning decision m4). "Ole" is the word these drafts use for "woe" and would sound like a lament, so Swahili uses the mocking "Aha!"; Balanced adds "ati", which repeats a claim in scorn, as in Matthew 27:40. Readable says "Jitazame!" (look at yourself), as the English does.

source.text: ὁμοίως καὶ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς ἐμπαίζοντες πρὸς ἀλλήλους μετὰ τῶν γραμματέων ἔλεγον· Ἄλλους ἔσωσεν, ἑαυτὸν οὐ δύναται σῶσαι·

records.literal_gloss: Likewise also the chief priests mocking to one another with the scribes were saying, Others he saved, himself not he is able to save.

en.L: Likewise the chief priests also, mocking [him] to one another with the scribes, were saying, "Others {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saved; {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cannot save.
en.B: The chief priests and the scribes mocked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the same way among themselves. "He saved other people," they said, "but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cannot save {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}!
en.R: The leading priests and the teachers of God's law also made fun of Jesus. They said to each other, "He saved other people, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cannot save {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}!

es.L: De igual manera también los jefes de los sacerdotes, burlándose entre sí con los escribas, decían: «A otros salvó; a {{deity_pronoun:sí|Sí}} mismo no se puede salvar.
es.B: Del mismo modo, los jefes de los sacerdotes y los escribas se burlaban de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} entre ellos. «Salvó a otros», decían, «¡pero a {{deity_pronoun:sí|Sí}} mismo no se puede salvar!
es.R: Los jefes de los sacerdotes y los maestros de la ley también se burlaban de Jesús. Se decían unos a otros: «¡Salvó a otros, pero no puede salvarse a {{deity_pronoun:sí|Sí}} mismo!

sw.L: Vivyo hivyo wakuu wa makuhani nao, wakidhihaki wao kwa wao pamoja na waandishi, walikuwa wakisema, "Wengine aliwaokoa; nafsi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} hawezi kuiokoa.
sw.B: Vivyo hivyo wakuu wa makuhani pamoja na waandishi walimdhihaki wao kwa wao. Walisema, "Aliwaokoa watu wengine, lakini hawezi kujiokoa {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}!
sw.R: Wakuu wa makuhani na walimu wa sheria nao walimcheka Yesu. Waliambiana, "Aliwaokoa watu wengine, lakini hawezi kujiokoa {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}!

decisions.choice: saved: rescued, and also healed
decisions.reason: The verb is used for Jesus' healings (5:34; 6:56; 10:52). The leaders admit that he rescued others.

decisions.choice: he cannot save himself: what they mean as scorn is true in another sense
decisions.reason: The leaders say he has no power. Mark's readers know he would not save himself, because he came to give his life (10:45).

decisions.choice: to one another: among themselves
decisions.reason: The leaders talk about Jesus to each other, not to him.

decisions.choice: himself
decisions.reason: The leaders speak of Jesus, so the pronouns for him take the setting for pronouns for Christ.

source.text: ὁ χριστὸς ὁ βασιλεὺς Ἰσραὴλ καταβάτω νῦν ἀπὸ τοῦ σταυροῦ, ἵνα ἴδωμεν καὶ πιστεύσωμεν.

records.literal_gloss: The Christ, the King of Israel, let him come down now from the cross, that we may see and believe.

en.L: Let the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe."
en.B: Let {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, the King of Israel, come down from the cross right now, so that we can see it and believe!"
en.R: This man says he is {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, the King of Israel. Let {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} come down from the cross now! When we see that, we will believe in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

es.L: Que el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, el Rey de Israel, baje ahora de la cruz, para que veamos y creamos».
es.B: ¡Que el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, el Rey de Israel, baje ahora mismo de la cruz, para que lo veamos y creamos!».
es.R: Este dice que es el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, el Rey de Israel. ¡Pues que baje ahora de la cruz! Cuando lo veamos, creeremos en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}».

sw.L: {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, Mfalme wa Israeli, ashuke sasa kutoka msalabani, ili tuone na kuamini."
sw.B: Basi {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, Mfalme wa Israeli, ashuke kutoka msalabani sasa hivi, ili tuone, tupate kuamini!"
sw.R: Mtu huyu anadai kuwa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, Mfalme wa Israeli. Basi ashuke kutoka msalabani sasa! Tukiona hivyo, tutamwamini."

decisions.choice: the Christ: the Messiah, God's anointed king
decisions.reason: The leaders use the title the high priest asked about (14:61). They mean it as scorn.

decisions.choice: the King of Israel: the title said by Jews
decisions.reason: Pilate and the soldiers said "King of the Jews", the way outsiders spoke. The leaders say "King of Israel", Israel's own name for itself.

decisions.choice: that we may see and believe: they demand a sign
decisions.reason: They ask for proof on their own terms, as the Pharisees asked for a sign in 8:11-12. Jesus refused then and does not answer now.

decisions.choice: This man says he is
alternatives: the Christ, the King of Israel
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the leaders are repeating the claim with scorn.

decisions.choice: believe in him
decisions.reason: Readable says whom they would believe. Mark leaves it unstated; it may mean believe in him or believe the claim.

decisions.choice: el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, with the article outside the span
decisions.reason: The leaders use the word as a title, "the Christ" (meaning decision m1). Spanish keeps the article with the title, so the setting changes only the noun, as the term sheet sets for "Cristo" used as a title.

source.text: καὶ οἱ συνεσταυρωμένοι σὺν αὐτῷ ὠνείδιζον αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And those crucified with him were insulting him.

en.L: And those crucified with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} were insulting {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Even the men crucified with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} heaped insults on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: The two men on the crosses next to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} also insulted {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Y los que estaban crucificados con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} injuriaban.
es.B: Hasta los que habían sido crucificados con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} cubrían de insultos.
es.R: Los dos hombres que estaban en las cruces junto a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} también {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} insultaban.

sw.L: Na wale waliosulubiwa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} walikuwa wakimtukana.
sw.B: Hata wale waliosulubiwa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} walimtupia matusi.
sw.R: Wale watu wawili waliokuwa kwenye misalaba karibu {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} nao walimtukana.

decisions.choice: were insulting: taunting, reproaching
decisions.reason: The verb means to heap scorn on someone.

decisions.choice: all mock him: passers-by, leaders and fellow victims
decisions.reason: Mark lists three groups who mock him, so that Jesus is left completely alone. Psalm 69:10 speaks of the insults of those who insult God falling on his servant.

decisions.choice: the two men on the crosses next to him
decisions.reason: Readable points back to the two of 15:27.

source.text: Καὶ γενομένης ὥρας ἕκτης σκότος ἐγένετο ἐφ’ ὅλην τὴν γῆν ἕως ὥρας ἐνάτης.

records.literal_gloss: And having come [the] hour sixth darkness came over all the land until [the] hour ninth.

en.L: And when the sixth hour came, darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.
en.B: At noon darkness fell over the whole land and lasted until three in the afternoon.
en.R: At twelve o'clock noon, the whole land became dark. It stayed dark until three o'clock in the afternoon.

es.L: Y llegada la hora sexta, hubo oscuridad sobre toda la tierra hasta la hora novena.
es.B: Al mediodía, la oscuridad cubrió toda la tierra y duró hasta las tres de la tarde.
es.R: A las doce del mediodía, toda la tierra se quedó a oscuras. Siguió oscuro hasta las tres de la tarde.

sw.L: Na ilipofika saa sita, giza likaja juu ya nchi yote mpaka saa tisa.
sw.B: Ilipofika saa sita mchana, giza liliifunika nchi yote mpaka saa tisa alasiri.
sw.R: Saa sita mchana nchi yote ikawa giza. Giza hilo likaendelea mpaka saa tisa alasiri.

decisions.choice: the sixth hour, the ninth hour: about noon and about three in the afternoon
alternatives: six and nine in the morning
decisions.reason: The hours were counted from sunrise, as in 15:25.

decisions.choice: the whole land: the land of Israel, or the whole earth
decisions.reason: The same word can mean land or earth. Mark does not say how far the darkness reached.

decisions.choice: darkness: a sign of God's judgment
decisions.reason: Amos 8:9 says that on that day God will make the sun go down at noon and darken the earth in broad daylight. Darkness also came on Egypt before the Passover (Exodus 10:22).

decisions.choice: the darkness was not an eclipse
decisions.reason: Passover fell at full moon, when an eclipse of the sun cannot happen. Mark does not say how the darkness came.

decisions.choice: noon, three in the afternoon (B); twelve o'clock noon, three o'clock in the afternoon (R)
alternatives: the sixth hour, the ninth hour
decisions.reason: As in 15:25, Literal keeps the ancient hours and the other levels give the time as we count it.

source.text: καὶ τῇ ἐνάτῃ ὥρᾳ ἐβόησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς φωνῇ μεγάλῃ· Ἐλωῒ ἐλωῒ λεμὰ σαβαχθάνι;

records.literal_gloss: And at the ninth hour cried out Jesus with a voice loud, Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?

en.L: And at the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, "Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?"
en.B: At three o'clock Jesus gave a loud shout: "Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?"
en.R: At three o'clock Jesus shouted loudly, "Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?"

es.L: Y a la hora novena Jesús gritó con gran voz: «Eloí, Eloí, ¿lema sabactani?».
