es.B: A las tres de la tarde Jesús lanzó un fuerte grito: «Eloí, Eloí, ¿lema sabactani?».
es.R: A las tres de la tarde Jesús gritó con fuerza: «Eloí, Eloí, ¿lema sabactani?».

sw.L: Na saa tisa Yesu alilia kwa sauti kuu, "Eloi, Eloi, lema sabakthani?"
sw.B: Saa tisa alasiri Yesu alilia kwa sauti kubwa, "Eloi, Eloi, lema sabakthani?"
sw.R: Saa tisa alasiri Yesu alipiga kelele kwa sauti kubwa, "Eloi, Eloi, lema sabakthani?"

decisions.choice: Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani: the first line of Psalm 22, in Aramaic
decisions.reason: Jesus prays the opening of Psalm 22 (22:2 in the Hebrew numbering) in Aramaic, the everyday language of Jews in his land. The psalm moves from a cry of abandonment to praise of God who rescues (Psalm 22:23-32). Mark has already echoed the psalm in 15:24 and 15:29.

decisions.choice: the cry: Jesus' real experience of being forsaken
alternatives: only a quotation with no feeling
God had stopped being his God
decisions.reason: Jesus still calls him "my God". The cry expresses deep anguish while holding on to God. Mark does not explain it further.

decisions.choice: cried out with a loud voice: shouted aloud
decisions.reason: The phrase shows strength, not the faint voice of a dying man.

decisions.choice: Eloi ... lema sabachthani: the spelling of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Eli ... lama sabachthani (the Hebrew form in some manuscripts)
decisions.reason: The manuscripts spell these words in several ways, some closer to the Hebrew of the psalm, as in Matthew 27:46. The SBLGNT has the Aramaic form. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani
decisions.reason: All levels keep the Aramaic words as Mark does, because Mark translates them in the next sentence and the misunderstanding in 15:35 depends on their sound. Balanced and Readable give the hour as three o'clock, as in 15:33.

decisions.choice: Eloí, Eloí, ¿lema sabactani? (every level)
alternatives: Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani (the English spelling)
decisions.reason: Mark gives Jesus's Aramaic words as they sounded (meaning decision m1) and translates them in the next sentence. Spanish spells them so that a Spanish reader says them as the Greek letters do: the accent keeps "Eloí" in three syllables, and "ct" stands for the English "chth". A reviewer should check the spelling.

decisions.choice: Eloi, Eloi, lema sabakthani? (every level)
alternatives: Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani (the English spelling)
decisions.reason: Mark gives Jesus's Aramaic words as they sounded (meaning decision m1) and translates them in the next sentence. Swahili spells them as it writes borrowed sounds: "k" for the Greek letter written "ch" in English, and "th" as in "thelathini". A reviewer should check the spelling.

source.text: ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον Ὁ θεός μου ὁ θεός μου, εἰς τί ἐγκατέλιπές με;

records.literal_gloss: Which is being translated, The God of me, the God of me, for what did you forsake me?

en.L: Which is translated, "My God, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} God, why have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} forsaken {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?"
en.B: That means, "My God, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} God, why did {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} abandon {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}?"
en.R: These words mean, "My God, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} God, why have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} left {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} all alone?"

es.L: Lo cual, traducido, es: «Dios mío, Dios {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}, ¿por qué {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} has abandonado?».
es.B: Esto significa: «Dios mío, Dios {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}, ¿por qué {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} abandonaste?».
es.R: Estas palabras quieren decir: «Dios mío, Dios {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}, ¿por qué {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} has dejado completamente solo?».

sw.L: Maana yake ikitafsiriwa ni, "Mungu wangu, Mungu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, kwa nini umeniacha?"
sw.B: Maana yake ni, "Mungu wangu, Mungu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, kwa nini umenitelekeza?"
sw.R: Maneno hayo maana yake ni, "Mungu wangu, Mungu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}, kwa nini umeniacha peke yangu kabisa?"

decisions.choice: forsaken: left behind, abandoned
decisions.reason: The verb means to leave someone in a time of need.

decisions.choice: for what: why
decisions.reason: The phrase asks why, in the words of Psalm 22:2.

decisions.choice: The God of me: my God, a form of address
decisions.reason: The article with the noun is used as a vocative, as often in Greek translated from Hebrew.

decisions.choice: left me all alone
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for forsaken. Literal keeps the traditional word.

decisions.choice: kwa nini umeniacha (L); kwa nini umenitelekeza (B); umeniacha peke yangu kabisa (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is to leave behind, to abandon (meaning decision m1), and the question asks why (meaning decision m2). Literal says "kuacha" (leave); Balanced "kutelekeza", to abandon someone without help, as the English "abandon"; Readable says he was left all alone, as the English does. "Kwa nini" is the plain "why".

source.text: καί τινες τῶν παρεστηκότων ἀκούσαντες ἔλεγον· Ἴδε Ἠλίαν φωνεῖ.

records.literal_gloss: And some of those standing by, having heard, were saying, Look, Elijah he calls.

en.L: And some of those standing by, when they heard [it], were saying, "Look, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is calling Elijah!"
en.B: Some of the bystanders heard it and said, "Listen, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is calling for Elijah!"
en.R: Some of the people standing there heard this. They said, "Listen! He is calling for Elijah!"

es.L: Y algunos de los que estaban allí, al oír[lo], decían: «Mira, llama a Elías».
es.B: Algunos de los que estaban cerca lo oyeron y dijeron: «{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}, está llamando a Elías».
es.R: Algunas de las personas que estaban allí lo oyeron. Dijeron: «¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}! ¡Está llamando a Elías!».

sw.L: Na baadhi ya wale waliosimama karibu, waliposikia, walikuwa wakisema, "Tazama, anamwita Eliya."
sw.B: Baadhi ya watu waliosimama pale walisikia, wakasema, "Sikilizeni, anamwita Eliya!"
sw.R: Baadhi ya watu waliokuwa wamesimama pale walisikia hivyo. Wakasema, "Sikilizeni! Anamwita Eliya!"

decisions.choice: Elijah: the cry sounded like Elijah's name
decisions.reason: In Hebrew "Eli" (my God) sounds close to the name Elijah. Many Jews believed Elijah would come to help the righteous in trouble, and that he would come before the end (9:11; Malachi 4:5).

decisions.choice: some of those standing by: Mark does not say who
decisions.reason: The talk about Elijah suggests Jews rather than Roman soldiers. Mark does not say whether they misheard or mocked on purpose.

decisions.choice: Look: listen, see
alternatives: a command to look at something
decisions.reason: The word draws attention, like "listen".

decisions.choice: Listen
decisions.reason: What drew attention was the cry, so Balanced and Readable use "Listen".

decisions.choice: Mira (L); {{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a singular "look" used as a set exclamation (meaning decision m3), which Literal keeps. The bystanders say it to one another, so Balanced and Readable use the plural, which takes the plural_you setting, and say "listen", since what they noticed was a cry.

source.text: δραμὼν δέ τις καὶ γεμίσας σπόγγον ὄξους περιθεὶς καλάμῳ ἐπότιζεν αὐτόν, λέγων· Ἄφετε ἴδωμεν εἰ ἔρχεται Ἠλίας καθελεῖν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Having run then someone and having filled a sponge with sour wine, having put [it] on a reed, was giving to drink him, saying, Leave, let us see if comes Elijah to take down him.

en.L: Then someone ran, filled a sponge with sour wine, put [it] on a reed, and was giving {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} a drink, saying, "Leave [him]; let us see if Elijah comes to take {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} down."
en.B: Someone ran and soaked a sponge in sour wine, put it on the end of a stick and offered it to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to drink. "Wait!" he said. "Let us see if Elijah will come and take {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} down."
en.R: One man ran and got a sponge. He filled it with cheap sour wine and put it on the end of a stick. He held it up to Jesus' mouth to drink. He said, "Wait! Let us see whether Elijah will come and take {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} down from the cross."

es.L: Y uno corrió, llenó una esponja de vino agrio, [la] puso en una caña y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} daba de beber, diciendo: «{{plural_you:Dejen|Dejad}}, veamos si viene Elías a bajarlo».
es.B: Alguien corrió, empapó una esponja en vino agrio, la puso en la punta de una vara y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} ofreció de beber. «¡{{plural_you:Esperen|Esperad}}!», dijo. «Veamos si viene Elías a bajarlo».
es.R: Un hombre corrió y tomó una esponja. La empapó en vino agrio barato y la puso en la punta de una vara. Luego la acercó a la boca de Jesús para que bebiera. Dijo: «¡{{plural_you:Esperen|Esperad}}! Vamos a ver si viene Elías a bajarlo de la cruz».

sw.L: Na mtu mmoja akakimbia, akajaza sifongo divai chungu, akaiweka juu ya mwanzi, akawa akimnywesha, akisema, "Acheni, tuone kama Eliya anakuja kumshusha."
sw.B: Mtu mmoja alikimbia, akachovya sifongo katika divai chungu, akaiweka kwenye ncha ya fimbo, akampa anywe. Akasema, "Ngojeni! Tuone kama Eliya atakuja kumshusha."
sw.R: Mtu mmoja alikimbia, akachukua sifongo. Akaijaza divai chungu ya bei rahisi, akaiweka kwenye ncha ya fimbo. Akaiinua mpaka kinywani mwa Yesu ili anywe. Akasema, "Ngojeni! Tuone kama Eliya atakuja kumshusha kutoka msalabani."

decisions.choice: sour wine: cheap wine gone sour, a common drink
decisions.reason: Soldiers and laborers drank this sharp wine mixed with water. It quenched thirst.

decisions.choice: sour wine to drink: Psalm 69:22
decisions.reason: The psalm says: for my thirst they gave me sour wine to drink.

decisions.choice: Leave: wait, let him be
alternatives: let him alone with no drink
decisions.reason: The word means let go or allow. Here it means hold off, wait and see. It can also be read as "let me" give him the drink.

decisions.choice: giving him a drink while mocking: whether kind or cruel is not clear
decisions.reason: The drink may have been meant to keep Jesus alive a little longer to see if Elijah came. The words sound like scorn. Mark does not say what the man meant.

decisions.choice: cheap; from the cross
decisions.reason: Readable says what kind of wine it was and where Jesus would be taken down from.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἀφεὶς φωνὴν μεγάλην ἐξέπνευσεν.

records.literal_gloss: But Jesus having let go a cry loud breathed his last.

en.L: But Jesus, letting out a loud cry, breathed [his] last.
en.B: But Jesus gave a loud cry and breathed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} last.
en.R: Then Jesus cried out loudly, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} died.

es.L: Pero Jesús, dando un fuerte grito, expiró.
es.B: Pero Jesús dio un fuerte grito y expiró.
es.R: Entonces Jesús gritó con fuerza y murió.

sw.L: Lakini Yesu, akiwa ametoa sauti kubwa, alitoa pumzi [yake] ya mwisho.
sw.B: Lakini Yesu alilia kwa sauti kubwa, akakata roho.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu alilia kwa sauti kubwa, akafa.

decisions.choice: breathed his last: died, gave up his breath
decisions.reason: The verb means to breathe out, a plain way of saying he died. It may also recall the Spirit who came into Jesus at his baptism (1:10), but the word itself means only to die.

decisions.choice: letting out a loud cry: a second loud cry, or the same cry as in 15:34
decisions.reason: Mark does not give the words of this cry. It is most likely a second cry at the moment of death.

decisions.choice: cry: a loud sound or shout
decisions.reason: The noun means a sound or a voice. Here it is a cry without words.

decisions.choice: he died
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plain word.

decisions.choice: expiró (L, B); murió (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is to breathe out, to breathe one's last (meaning decision m1). "Expirar" says this in one word and comes from the same picture; Readable says plainly that he died, as the English does.

decisions.choice: alitoa pumzi [yake] ya mwisho (L); akakata roho (B); akafa (R)
decisions.reason: Mark's verb is to breathe out, to breathe one's last (meaning decision m1), not John's verb of handing over the spirit. Literal keeps the picture of the last breath; Balanced uses "kukata roho", the everyday Swahili idiom for dying at the last breath; Readable says plainly that he died, as the English does.

source.text: καὶ τὸ καταπέτασμα τοῦ ναοῦ ἐσχίσθη εἰς δύο ἀπ’ ἄνωθεν ἕως κάτω.

records.literal_gloss: And the curtain of the sanctuary was torn into two from top to bottom.

en.L: And the curtain of the sanctuary was torn in two from top to bottom.
en.B: And the curtain in the sanctuary was split in two from top to bottom.
en.R: At that moment the curtain in the temple was torn in two pieces, from the top all the way down to the bottom.

es.L: Y la cortina del santuario fue rasgada en dos, de arriba hasta abajo.
es.B: Y la cortina del santuario fue rasgada en dos de arriba abajo.
es.R: En ese mismo momento, la cortina del templo fue rasgada en dos pedazos, desde arriba hasta abajo.

sw.L: Na pazia la patakatifu likapasuliwa vipande viwili kutoka juu hadi chini.
sw.B: Pazia la patakatifu likapasuliwa vipande viwili, kuanzia juu mpaka chini.
sw.R: Wakati huo huo pazia la hekalu lilipasuliwa vipande viwili, kuanzia juu kabisa mpaka chini.

decisions.choice: was torn: ripped apart, the same verb as at Jesus' baptism
decisions.reason: Mark uses this verb only here and at 1:10, where the heavens were torn open. At the start and the end of Jesus' work, God tears something open.

decisions.choice: was torn: a passive, God is the one who tore it
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the actor unnamed, and "from top to bottom" shows the tear came from above.

decisions.choice: the curtain of the sanctuary: most likely the inner curtain before the Most Holy Place
alternatives: the outer curtain at the entrance to the sanctuary
decisions.reason: The sanctuary had two great curtains. The inner one closed off the Most Holy Place, where only the high priest went once a year (Exodus 26:31-33; Hebrews 10:19-20). The outer one hung at the entrance and could be seen from outside. Mark does not say which.

decisions.choice: the torn curtain: a sign of God's action at Jesus' death
decisions.reason: Mark does not explain it. It may show that the way to God is open, or announce judgment on the temple, which Jesus foretold (13:2). Both may be in view.

decisions.choice: sanctuary
decisions.reason: The word means the sanctuary building itself, not the whole temple area. Readable says "the temple".

decisions.choice: fue rasgada (every level)
decisions.reason: The verb is passive, and the one who tore the curtain is God (meaning decision m2). "Se rasgó" would say only that it tore, so every level keeps the passive, as the English "was torn" does.

decisions.choice: pazia la patakatifu (L, B), pazia la hekalu (R); likapasuliwa (passive)
decisions.reason: The verb is passive, and the one who tore the curtain is God (meaning decision m2), so every level says "-pasuliwa" (was torn) rather than "-pasuka" (tore). "Patakatifu" names the sanctuary itself, as the English does at Literal and Balanced; Readable says "hekalu", as the English "temple".

source.text: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ κεντυρίων ὁ παρεστηκὼς ἐξ ἐναντίας αὐτοῦ ὅτι οὕτως ἐξέπνευσεν εἶπεν· Ἀληθῶς οὗτος ὁ ἄνθρωπος υἱὸς θεοῦ ἦν.

records.literal_gloss: Having seen then the centurion standing by from opposite him that thus he breathed his last, he said, Truly this the man God's Son was.

en.L: And when the centurion who stood by facing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} saw that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} breathed [his] last in this way, he said, "Truly this man was God's Son!"
en.B: The centurion standing in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} saw how {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} died, and he said, "This man really was God's Son!"
en.R: A Roman army officer was standing in front of Jesus. When he saw how Jesus died, he said, "This man really was God's Son!"

es.L: Y el centurión que estaba frente a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, viendo que así había expirado, dijo: «Verdaderamente este hombre era Hijo de Dios».
es.B: El centurión que estaba frente a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} vio cómo murió, y dijo: «¡De verdad este hombre era Hijo de Dios!».
es.R: Un oficial del ejército romano estaba de pie frente a Jesús. Cuando vio cómo murió Jesús, dijo: «¡De verdad este hombre era Hijo de Dios!».

sw.L: Na yule akida aliyesimama akimkabili, alipoona kwamba alitoa pumzi ya mwisho hivyo, alisema, "Kweli mtu huyu alikuwa Mwana wa Mungu!"
sw.B: Akida aliyesimama mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} alipoona jinsi alivyokufa, alisema, "Hakika mtu huyu alikuwa Mwana wa Mungu!"
sw.R: Afisa wa jeshi la Kirumi alikuwa amesimama mbele ya Yesu. Alipoona jinsi Yesu alivyokufa, alisema, "Hakika mtu huyu alikuwa Mwana wa Mungu!"

decisions.choice: God's Son: the Son of God, the title Mark gives Jesus
alternatives: a son of God, a divine or godlike man in the centurion's own Roman sense
decisions.reason: The Greek has no article, so it could mean "a son of God". But a title placed before the verb often lacks the article and is still definite, and Mark began his book with Jesus as God's Son (1:1). God called him "my Son" (1:11; 9:7). For Mark, the first human to say it is a Gentile soldier at the cross. What the centurion himself understood is less certain.

decisions.choice: that he breathed his last in this way: the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: that he cried out in this way and breathed his last
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "cried out and". The SBLGNT reads the shorter text. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: centurion: a Roman officer over about a hundred soldiers
decisions.reason: Mark uses the Latin title. He was in charge of the execution.

decisions.choice: was: the centurion speaks of Jesus as now dead
alternatives: he was so only in the past
decisions.reason: The past tense fits a man speaking of one who has just died.

decisions.choice: God's Son
decisions.reason: All levels say "God's Son", which keeps the same openness as the Greek and does not settle the question that the meaning decision leaves open. Readable says "a Roman army officer" for centurion.

decisions.choice: centurión (L, B), oficial del ejército romano (R); era Hijo de Dios, with no article
decisions.reason: The Greek has no article, and the officer's words may be the full title Mark gives Jesus (meaning decision m1, uncertain). Spanish leaves out the article after "era" naturally, so both readings stay open, as the English "God's Son" does. The officer is named as in Matthew 8 and 27 (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: akida (L, B), afisa wa jeshi la Kirumi (R); Mwana wa Mungu
decisions.reason: The officer over about a hundred soldiers (meaning decision m3), named as in Matthew 8 and 27. Swahili has no article, so "Mwana wa Mungu" leaves open whether he spoke the full title (meaning decision m1, uncertain), as the English "God's Son" does.

source.text: Ἦσαν δὲ καὶ γυναῖκες ἀπὸ μακρόθεν θεωροῦσαι, ἐν αἷς καὶ Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ Μαρία ἡ Ἰακώβου τοῦ μικροῦ καὶ Ἰωσῆτος μήτηρ καὶ Σαλώμη, αἳ ὅτε ἦν ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ ἠκολούθουν αὐτῷ καὶ διηκόνουν αὐτῷ, καὶ ἄλλαι πολλαὶ αἱ συναναβᾶσαι αὐτῷ εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.

records.literal_gloss: Now there were also women from afar watching, among whom also Mary the Magdalene and Mary the of James the small and of Joses mother and Salome, \v 41 who, when he was in Galilee, were following him and serving him, and other many who came up with him to Jerusalem.

en.L: Now there were also women watching from a distance, among whom [were] also Mary the Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome, \v 41 who, when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was in Galilee, used to follow {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and serve {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and many other [women] who had come up with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to Jerusalem.
en.B: Women were also there, looking on from far off, among them Mary Magdalene; Mary, mother of the younger James and of Joses; and Salome. \v 41 In Galilee they had followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and looked after {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} needs. Many other women were there as well, who had come with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} up to Jerusalem.
en.R: Some women were watching from far away. Mary from the town of Magdala was there. So was another Mary, the mother of the younger James and of Joses. Salome was there too. \v 41 These women had followed Jesus in Galilee and had taken care of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Many other women were there also. They had come with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to Jerusalem.

es.L: Y había también mujeres mirando desde lejos, entre las cuales [estaban] también María la Magdalena, y María la madre de Santiago el menor y de Joset, y Salomé, \v 41 las cuales, cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} estaba en Galilea, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} seguían y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} servían, y muchas otras que habían subido con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a Jerusalén.
es.B: También había allí unas mujeres que miraban desde lejos. Entre ellas estaban María Magdalena, María la madre de Santiago el menor y de Joset, y Salomé. \v 41 En Galilea {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} habían seguido y habían atendido a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} necesidades. También estaban allí muchas otras mujeres que habían subido con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a Jerusalén.
es.R: Algunas mujeres miraban desde lejos. Allí estaba María, la del pueblo de Magdala. También estaba otra María, la madre de Santiago el menor y de Joset. Y estaba Salomé. \v 41 Estas mujeres habían seguido a Jesús en Galilea y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} habían cuidado. También estaban allí muchas otras mujeres que habían venido con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a Jerusalén.

sw.L: Na walikuwapo pia wanawake wakitazama kwa mbali, ambao miongoni mwao [walikuwa] pia Mariamu Magdalene, na Mariamu mama wa Yakobo mdogo na wa Yose, na Salome, \v 41 ambao, alipokuwa Galilaya, walikuwa wakimfuata na kumhudumia, na wengine wengi waliopanda pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} kwenda Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Walikuwako pia wanawake waliokuwa wakitazama kwa mbali. Miongoni mwao walikuwa Mariamu Magdalene, Mariamu mama wa Yakobo mdogo na wa Yose, na Salome. \v 41 Alipokuwa Galilaya, wanawake hao walimfuata na kumtimizia mahitaji {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Walikuwako pia wanawake wengine wengi waliopanda pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} kwenda Yerusalemu.
sw.R: Wanawake kadhaa walikuwa wakitazama kwa mbali. Mariamu wa mji wa Magdala alikuwa pale. Mariamu mwingine, mama wa Yakobo mdogo na wa Yose, alikuwa pale pia. Salome naye alikuwa pale. \v 41 Wanawake hawa walimfuata Yesu huko Galilaya na kumtunza. Wanawake wengine wengi walikuwa pale pia. Hao walikuwa wamekuja pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} Yerusalemu.

decisions.choice: from a distance: perhaps Psalm 38:12
decisions.reason: The psalm says that friends and neighbors stand far off. The women were at least present when the men had fled (14:50).

decisions.choice: Mary the Magdalene: Mary from Magdala
decisions.reason: Magdala was a town on the west shore of the Sea of Galilee. Luke 8:2 says seven demons had gone out of her.

decisions.choice: the younger: literally the small, either younger or short
decisions.reason: The word means small. It may mark him as younger than another James, or as short. It sets him apart from James the son of Zebedee.

decisions.choice: Mary the mother of James and Joses: not Jesus' mother, though Jesus had brothers named James and Joses
decisions.reason: Mark 6:3 names Jesus' brothers as James and Joses. But Mark would hardly call Jesus' mother only "the mother of James and Joses" here. Most likely this is another Mary.

decisions.choice: serving him: caring for his needs, providing for him
decisions.reason: The verb means to serve or wait on. Luke 8:3 says such women provided for Jesus from their own means. It is the verb of 10:45.

decisions.choice: Mary from the town of Magdala
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name. Literal keeps the article, "the Magdalene", as the Greek has it.

decisions.choice: Joset
decisions.reason: The Greek name is a short form of Joseph. Spanish often writes it "José", but this chapter also names Joseph of Arimathea (15:43, 45), and in 15:47 "María la madre de José" would read as his mother. "Joset" keeps the two men apart. The same in 15:47.

source.text: Καὶ ἤδη ὀψίας γενομένης, ἐπεὶ ἦν παρασκευή, ὅ ἐστιν προσάββατον, ἐλθὼν Ἰωσὴφ ὁ ἀπὸ Ἁριμαθαίας εὐσχήμων βουλευτής, ὃς καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν προσδεχόμενος τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ, τολμήσας εἰσῆλθεν πρὸς τὸν Πιλᾶτον καὶ ᾐτήσατο τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And already evening having come, since it was Preparation, which is the day before Sabbath, \v 43 having come Joseph the [one] from Arimathea, a respected council member, who also himself was waiting for the kingdom of God, having dared went in to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.

en.L: And when evening had already come, since it was [the] Preparation, that is, the day before [the] Sabbath, \v 43 Joseph from Arimathea came, a respected council member, who himself was also waiting for the kingdom of God, and taking courage he went in to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
en.B: Evening was already coming on. Since it was the day of Preparation, the day before the Sabbath, \v 43 Joseph from Arimathea came. He was a respected member of the Council who was also looking for the kingdom of God. He boldly went in to Pilate and requested the body of Jesus.
en.R: By now it was evening. It was Preparation Day, the day before the Sabbath. \v 43 A man named Joseph came. He was from the town of Arimathea. He was an important member of the Jewish council, and he was waiting for the kingdom of God to come. Joseph was brave enough to go to Pilate and ask him for Jesus' body.

es.L: Y como ya había llegado la tarde, puesto que era [la] Preparación, es decir, la víspera del sábado, \v 43 vino José de Arimatea, un consejero respetado, que también él mismo esperaba el reino de Dios, y, atreviéndose, entró adonde estaba Pilato y pidió el cuerpo de Jesús.
es.B: Ya caía la tarde. Como era el día de la Preparación, es decir, la víspera del sábado, \v 43 llegó José de Arimatea. Era un miembro respetado del Consejo, que también esperaba el reino de Dios. Se armó de valor, se presentó ante Pilato y le pidió el cuerpo de Jesús.
es.R: Ya era la tarde. Era el día de la Preparación, el día antes del sábado. \v 43 Llegó un hombre llamado José. Era del pueblo de Arimatea. Era un miembro importante del Consejo Supremo de los judíos, y esperaba que llegara el reino de Dios. José se armó de valor, fue a ver a Pilato y le pidió el cuerpo de Jesús.

sw.L: Na jioni ilipokwisha kufika, kwa kuwa ilikuwa [siku ya] Maandalio, yaani, siku kabla ya Sabato, \v 43 Yusufu wa Arimathaya alikuja, mjumbe wa baraza aliyeheshimika, ambaye yeye mwenyewe pia alikuwa akiutazamia ufalme wa Mungu, akajipa moyo, akaingia kwa Pilato, akaomba mwili wa Yesu.
sw.B: Jioni ilikuwa imekwisha kuingia. Kwa kuwa ilikuwa siku ya Maandalio, yaani siku kabla ya Sabato, \v 43 Yusufu wa Arimathaya alikuja. Alikuwa mjumbe wa baraza aliyeheshimika, ambaye naye alikuwa akiutazamia ufalme wa Mungu. Akajipa ujasiri, akaingia kwa Pilato, akaomba apewe mwili wa Yesu.
sw.R: Ilikuwa tayari jioni. Ilikuwa siku ya Maandalio, yaani siku kabla ya Sabato. \v 43 Mtu mmoja aitwaye Yusufu alikuja. Alikuwa wa mji wa Arimathaya. Alikuwa mjumbe muhimu wa baraza kuu la Wayahudi, naye alikuwa akingojea ufalme wa Mungu uje. Yusufu alikuwa na ujasiri wa kwenda kwa Pilato na kumwomba mwili wa Yesu.

decisions.choice: Preparation, the day before the Sabbath: Friday
decisions.reason: Mark explains the word for non-Jewish readers. The Sabbath began at sunset on Friday, and no work could be done then, so the body had to be buried before dark (Deuteronomy 21:22-23).

decisions.choice: evening: late afternoon, toward sunset
decisions.reason: The word covers the time before and after sunset. Here the Sabbath had not yet begun.

decisions.choice: a respected council member: a member of the Sanhedrin
decisions.reason: Luke 23:50-51 says Joseph was a member of the council who had not agreed with its decision.

decisions.choice: waiting for the kingdom of God: looking for God's reign to come
decisions.reason: Mark does not call him a disciple, but he shared the hope Jesus preached (1:15). Matthew 27:57 and John 19:38 say he was a disciple.

decisions.choice: taking courage: daring
decisions.reason: To ask for the body of a man condemned as a rebel could put Joseph in danger and set him apart from the council.

decisions.choice: the long sentence broken into several
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break Mark's long sentence. Readable says "Jewish council" and explains Arimathea as a town.

decisions.choice: siku ya Maandalio, siku kabla ya Sabato
decisions.reason: The day on which everything was made ready for the Sabbath, that is, Friday (meaning decision m1). Every level keeps the name and Mark's own explanation, as the English does, rather than naming the weekday.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος ἐθαύμασεν εἰ ἤδη τέθνηκεν, καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τὸν κεντυρίωνα ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτὸν εἰ πάλαι ἀπέθανεν·

records.literal_gloss: And Pilate wondered if already he had died, and having summoned the centurion he asked him whether long ago he died.

en.L: And Pilate wondered whether {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had already died, and summoning the centurion, he asked him whether {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had died long [ago].
en.B: Pilate was surprised that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could already be dead. He called the centurion and asked him whether {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had been dead for some time.
en.R: Pilate was surprised that Jesus was already dead. So he called the army officer and asked him whether Jesus had been dead long.

es.L: Y Pilato se extrañó de que ya hubiera muerto, y, llamando al centurión, le preguntó si había muerto hacía mucho.
es.B: Pilato se sorprendió de que ya estuviera muerto. Llamó al centurión y le preguntó si hacía rato que había muerto.
es.R: Pilato se sorprendió de que Jesús ya estuviera muerto. Así que llamó al oficial y le preguntó si hacía mucho que Jesús había muerto.

sw.L: Naye Pilato alishangaa kama tayari amekwisha kufa, na akimwita akida, akamwuliza kama alikuwa amekufa zamani.
sw.B: Pilato alishangaa kwamba alikuwa amekwisha kufa. Akamwita akida, akamwuliza kama alikuwa amekufa muda mrefu.
sw.R: Pilato alishangaa kwamba Yesu alikuwa amekwisha kufa. Kwa hiyo alimwita yule afisa, akamwuliza kama Yesu alikuwa amekufa muda mrefu.

decisions.choice: Pilate was surprised: crucified men often lived for days
decisions.reason: Death on a cross could take a long time. Jesus died after about six hours (15:25, 34-37).

decisions.choice: long ago: for some time, or already
decisions.reason: The word means long ago. Here it asks whether Jesus had been dead for a while. Some manuscripts read "already". Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: had died: the perfect, he was dead
decisions.reason: Pilate wonders whether Jesus was truly dead. His question to the centurion confirms the death.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus where "he" could be Pilate or the centurion.

source.text: καὶ γνοὺς ἀπὸ τοῦ κεντυρίωνος ἐδωρήσατο τὸ πτῶμα τῷ Ἰωσήφ.

records.literal_gloss: And having learned from the centurion, he granted the corpse to Joseph.

en.L: And when he learned [it] from the centurion, he granted the corpse to Joseph.
en.B: When the centurion told him, he gave the body to Joseph.
en.R: The officer told Pilate that Jesus was dead. So Pilate let Joseph have the body.

es.L: Y, informado por el centurión, concedió el cadáver a José.
es.B: Cuando el centurión se lo confirmó, le dio el cuerpo a José.
es.R: El oficial le dijo a Pilato que Jesús estaba muerto. Entonces Pilato dejó que José se llevara el cuerpo.

sw.L: Naye, alipokwisha kujua kutoka kwa akida, akamtunukia Yusufu maiti.
sw.B: Alipoarifiwa na akida, alimpa Yusufu mwili.
sw.R: Yule afisa alimwambia Pilato kwamba Yesu amekufa. Kwa hiyo Pilato alimruhusu Yusufu auchukue mwili.

decisions.choice: corpse: a dead body
decisions.reason: Joseph asked for the body (15:43). Pilate grants the corpse, a word that makes the death certain.

decisions.choice: granted: gave as a favor
decisions.reason: The verb means to give freely. Pilate did not ask a price.

decisions.choice: the body
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "body", the natural word in English. Literal keeps "corpse" to show the change of word.

source.text: καὶ ἀγοράσας σινδόνα καθελὼν αὐτὸν ἐνείλησεν τῇ σινδόνι καὶ ἔθηκεν αὐτὸν ἐν μνημείῳ ὃ ἦν λελατομημένον ἐκ πέτρας, καὶ προσεκύλισεν λίθον ἐπὶ τὴν θύραν τοῦ μνημείου.

records.literal_gloss: And having bought linen, having taken down him, he wrapped [him] in the linen and laid him in a tomb which was cut out of rock, and he rolled a stone against the door of the tomb.

en.L: And having bought linen, he took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} down, wrapped [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] in the linen, and laid {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in a tomb that had been cut out of rock, and he rolled a stone against the door of the tomb.
en.B: Joseph bought a linen cloth, took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} down and wrapped {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in it. He laid {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in a tomb that had been carved out of the rock, and he rolled a stone over the entrance of the tomb.
en.R: Joseph bought a long cloth made of linen. He took Jesus' body down from the cross and wrapped it in the cloth. Then he placed it in a tomb cut into the side of a rock. He rolled a large stone in front of the opening to close the tomb.

es.L: Y, habiendo comprado una sábana de lino, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} bajó, [{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}] envolvió en la sábana y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} puso en un sepulcro que estaba excavado en la roca, e hizo rodar una piedra contra la puerta del sepulcro.
es.B: José compró una sábana de lino, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} bajó y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} envolvió en ella. Luego {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} puso en un sepulcro excavado en la roca e hizo rodar una piedra hasta la entrada del sepulcro.
es.R: José compró una tela larga de lino. Bajó de la cruz el cuerpo de Jesús y lo envolvió en la tela. Después lo colocó en una tumba excavada en la roca. Hizo rodar una piedra grande hasta la entrada para cerrar la tumba.

sw.L: Naye, akiisha kununua sanda ya kitani, akamshusha, akamfunga kwa ile sanda, akamweka katika kaburi lililokuwa limechongwa katika mwamba, akavingirisha jiwe mpaka mlangoni mwa kaburi.
sw.B: Yusufu alinunua sanda ya kitani, akamshusha, akamfunga kwa sanda hiyo. Akamweka katika kaburi lililochongwa katika mwamba, kisha akavingirisha jiwe kufunga mlango wa kaburi.
sw.R: Yusufu alinunua kitambaa kirefu cha kitani. Akaushusha mwili wa Yesu kutoka msalabani, akauzungushia kile kitambaa. Kisha akauweka ndani ya kaburi lililochongwa katika mwamba. Akavingirisha jiwe kubwa mbele ya mlango ili kulifunga kaburi.

decisions.choice: linen: a linen sheet for burial
decisions.reason: The dead were wrapped in linen cloth. Joseph bought it, though it was nearly the Sabbath.

decisions.choice: a tomb cut out of rock: a chamber cut into a rock face
alternatives: a grave dug in the ground
decisions.reason: Wealthy families in Jerusalem had tombs cut into the hillside, with shelves for bodies inside.

decisions.choice: a stone against the door: a large stone that closed the entrance
decisions.reason: Such stones were often round and rolled in a groove. Mark says later that it was very large (16:4).

decisions.choice: having taken him down: Joseph saw to it, likely with help
decisions.reason: Mark names Joseph as the one who acted. He may have had servants or others to help.

decisions.choice: Jesus' body; it
decisions.reason: Readable speaks of the body, so it uses "it" for the body. The pronoun is not one for Jesus himself.

decisions.choice: sepulcro (L, B); tumba (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts, as in Mark 16: "sepulcro" at Literal and Balanced, the everyday "tumba" at Readable.

source.text: ἡ δὲ Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ Μαρία ἡ Ἰωσῆτος ἐθεώρουν ποῦ τέθειται.

records.literal_gloss: And Mary the Magdalene and Mary the [mother] of Joses were watching where he had been laid.

en.L: And Mary the Magdalene and Mary the [mother] of Joses were watching where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had been laid.
en.B: Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses were watching to see where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was placed.
en.R: Mary from Magdala and Mary the mother of Joses watched. They saw where Jesus' body was put.

es.L: Y María la Magdalena y María la [madre] de Joset miraban dónde había sido puesto.
es.B: María Magdalena y María la madre de Joset miraban dónde {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} ponían.
es.R: María, la del pueblo de Magdala, y María, la madre de Joset, estaban mirando. Vieron dónde ponían el cuerpo de Jesús.

sw.L: Naye Mariamu Magdalene na Mariamu [mama] wa Yose walikuwa wakitazama mahali alipolazwa.
sw.B: Mariamu Magdalene na Mariamu mama wa Yose walikuwa wakitazama ili waone mahali alipowekwa.
sw.R: Mariamu wa mji wa Magdala na Mariamu mama wa Yose walitazama. Waliona mahali mwili wa Yesu ulipowekwa.

decisions.choice: were watching: they saw and took note
decisions.reason: The tense pictures them watching. They knew the place when they came back (16:1-2).

decisions.choice: had been laid: the perfect, he lay there
decisions.reason: The form shows where Jesus now lay.

decisions.choice: Mary of Joses: the mother of Joses
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "of Joses". From 15:40 she is his mother.

decisions.choice: the [mother] (L); the mother (B)
decisions.reason: 15:40 shows the relationship, so it is supplied.
